"O best of the twice-born, let that which you desire from me be granted; since, my child, this hymn has been composed by you with such purity. (14)
Agastya said: "O Mother, benefactress of the gods, if a boon is to be granted, let this river be increased in the world so that she may bring fear to all people. (15)
"By her this entire universe has been inundated; therefore, accept her. Thus was she entreated at that time by the great seer.
Then, O Vyāsa, that virtuous woman arrived at the auspicious Mahākālavana and spoke these truthful words of consolation to Agasti: || 17 ||
"O Sage, I shall quickly restrain the supreme goddess as she grows; until that time, the great mountain named Vindhya shall not rise. (18)
"O best of sages, as long as you remain at the gate of Trikūṭa, you shall be constantly intent upon the task of the gods in that most excellent southern direction. (19)

O best of sages, this city is indeed Kuśasthalī—highly meritorious, pure, and a destroyer of sins; it is renowned throughout the three worlds. It is there that I dwell for a long time together with my mothers.
There too, you shall always attain sovereignty over the field of accomplishment (siddhakṣetra), which is pure merit, stainless, possessing pure water, and renowned.
In that sacred place where the dwellings of the meritorious are located and where crores of goddesses reside, men, having bathed in that tirtha, become pure and composed.
They worship me indeed with devotion through incense, lamps, fire-offerings, and libations; and they should duly feed the twice-born with meals of milk, sugar-candy, ghee, and other delicacies.
For them, nothing whatsoever in the three worlds is difficult to obtain—whether it be wealth, grain, land, sovereignty, sons, wives, or other forms of prosperity. (24)
They obtain various enjoyments difficult even for the gods to attain; they have no fear from enemies, nor from robbers, nor from the king. (25)
Neither by weapons, fire, nor floods of water shall he ever perish; having lived for eternal years in this world, he shall be long-lived and wise. (26)
With his soul purified of all sins, he shall go to the city of Śiva upon death; thus, O Vyāsa, having reached the beautiful and auspicious city of Ujjayinī.
At that time, the goddess Vindhyavāsinī was constantly residing there; having bathed in that tīrtha, a man is liberated from all sins. || 28 ||
Women afflicted by the defects of menstruation, barren women, those who are like crows or cranes, the unfortunate, those devoid of virtue, and those bereft of all desired objects; || 29 ||
Having bathed in the Vimalodā and beheld the Goddess who dwells on the Vindhya mountains, they are liberated from all defects; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Childless women shall obtain sons, and maidens shall obtain a hero as a husband; all auspicious fortune, which grants the boon of every desire, is thereby attained.
The learned Brahmin becomes possessed of knowledge, the Kṣatriya becomes victorious, the Vaiśya becomes enriched with abundant profit, and the Śūdra enjoys happiness. (32)
By reading or even by hearing this meritorious narrative, which grants the boon of all desires, one obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows.
Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, there is another sacred ford (tīrtha) arising from the confluence of the Kṣātā, where one is liberated from great sins merely by bathing. || 1 ||
When the new moon coincides with Saturday, one who is composed in mind should perform a śrāddha ceremony and offer water with sesame seeds for the sake of the ancestors. || 2 ||
One should behold the god Śanaiścara, the supreme stationary liṅga; for him, the affliction caused by Saturn shall never occur at any time.
Vyāsa said: A great sacred site (tīrtha) has been described in the auspicious Mahākālavana; O ascetic, I desire to hear more about it in detail.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O best of the twice-born, to this auspicious ancient tale (paurāṇikī kathā), by the mere hearing of which the destruction of great sins occurs. (5)
O sinless one, in ancient times, the three rivers—the Revā, the Carmaṇvatī, and the Kṣātā—were born on earth from Amarakaṇṭaka as sanctifiers of the three worlds.
Meritorious, possessing meritorious waters, delightful, pure, and destroyers of sin, these rivers purify all people through bathing and drinking.
Once, in a beautiful grove in the excellent field of Māndhātṛ, they rejoiced together, thrilled with a mutual desire for victory over one another.
Indeed, due to the occurrence of some fault, a mutual separation arose; she abandoned her union with the Revā and, having split the excellent Vindhya mountain, [proceeded].
In the delightful Mahākālavana flows the excellent river Śiprā, which is greatly meritorious; for this city is indeed like Amarāvatī. || 10 ||
The most excellent and supreme among all sacred fords is known by the name Rudrasaras; it eternally bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and is frequented by hosts of perfected sages.

Having arrived there in ancient times, the Kṣātā took refuge at the confluence of the Śiprā; there a supreme holy site arose, known as Kṣātāsaṅgama, where Vibhāvasu was immediately declared to have become one whose impurities were shaken off.
Vyāsa said: How was it that Sūrya, as you have described, became free from passion (viraja) in ancient times? I wish to know this from you, O best among the knowers of Brahman. (13)
Sanatkumāra said: In ancient times, Tvaṣṭṛ gave his own daughter Sāvitrī to Anusūrya.
Constantly devoted to her husband’s dharma, she served the Eye of the World; from her and Vibhāvasu, the witness of the world, a pair of twins was born.
Yama, the son of Vivasvat, was born, as was Yamunā, the purifier of the world; then Tvaṣṭṛ spoke these truthful words to his own shadow.
"This pair has been placed by me in your lap; you must protect them until they have reached their father's house, O Chāyā. (17)
"O Chāyā, remain constantly devoted to the worship of the Sun within my abode; never speak of me to the Sun when he has come to your father's house. (18)
Having thus made this agreement, the young Sāvitrī then went to her father’s house, overwhelmed with fear of the Sun.
Immediately restrained by her father, she assumed the form of a mare and roamed through the delightful forest, which abounded in water and lush grass.
Once, when Vaivasvata was hungry and begged for food, she immediately gave boiled rice to him as he requested it.
Then the shadow, struck by his foot, cursed him, saying: "Since you have struck me with your foot out of childishness," (22)
"Therefore, you too shall become lame in one foot; of this there is no doubt. Thus cursed, overcome by pain and afflicted by grief, he lamented.
In the meantime, O Vyāsa, the sun, moving as a planet, traversed the earth and pervaded all the worlds.
And seeing his son lame, Vibhāvasu spoke thus: "What is this affliction of yours, my child? O sinless one, from where did you obtain this?"
When he was thus questioned by Sūrya, the illuminator of the world, Yama, the lord of Saṃyaminī, spoke these words in a faltering voice.
"O Lord, for my morning meal, I requested food from my mother; she did not give it quickly, and out of childishness, she struck me. (27)
"My feet have instantly withered through the defeat caused by my mother's curse. Hearing that, Ravi fell into a state of stupor and became absorbed in meditation.
"This cause of my mother's curse is truly wondrous"; having reflected thus for a long time, the sun-rayed one came to understand it. (29)
"This is not that daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ with beautiful outer corners of her eyes, the purifier of the world; who is she, from where has she come, and who are you, O lady of pure smiles? (30)
Chāyā said: "O great king, I am not Anusūryā; I am her own shadow-born sister. She has indeed gone to her father's house, and by her, O sinless one, I was forbidden [to follow]."
"O Lord, nothing at all must be said by me to Savitṛ under any circumstances; this is my vow, O Master, and for that reason I have observed silence."
Having heard that, the Lord Bhānu, filled with great wrath, went in haste to the presence of Tvaṣṭṛ, abiding in anger. || 33 ||
Seeing him, Tvaṣṭṛ, the grandfather of the worlds, rose up suddenly and honored him with water for the feet, the arghya offering, water for sipping, and the madhuparka.
Having bowed at his feet and circumambulated him with great reverence, he spoke in a sweet voice: "What pleasing service may we do for you? (35)
The Sun said: "O father, where is Sāvitrī, accompanied by Anasūyā, who does what is pleasing to me? She has come to your house, O dear one, following my path. (36)
Tvaṣṭṛ said: "O dear one, we do not know where my beloved daughter has gone. When these words were spoken by Tvaṣṭṛ, the Sun was deeply troubled in mind.
"What shall I do? Where shall I go? And where is she who is most dear to me?"—as he was speaking thus, Tvaṣṭṛ then spoke these words.
"Your wife, overwhelmed by your splendor, has fled somewhere broken and powerless; if she is dear to you, then pacify your splendor. (39)
Sūrya said: "O my great-grandfather, if this brilliance of mine is thus unbearable to you, then do exactly as you deem best so that it may become bearable."
Having heard these words of Sūrya, Sudarśana was shaved with a razor-edge; through that friction, he became exceedingly light and pure. (41)
By the mere act of rubbing that [stone], Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for Vivasvat the Sudarśana discus from the grit, and various kinds of gems from the sand.
Then Tvaṣṭṛ spoke these sweet words in the presence of Sūrya: "In the beautiful Mahākāla forest, there is a mare named Gīraṇī. (43)
"O best of gods, take it! Let him go quickly to the grassy meadow where the Śiprā, the most excellent of rivers, meets with the Kṣātā. (44)
Where there is a meeting of both, there is liberation without a doubt; there you will find that fortunate wife, of this there is no doubt. (45)
Having heard these words of his, Savitṛ, the scorcher of all, went to that forest where the purifying [shrine] of Mahākāla is located.
Where the milk-abounding Śiprā flows, joined with the confluence of the Kṣātā, there is both worldly enjoyment and liberation, along with the acquisition of wealth and grain. (47)
Having arrived there, Hari, assuming the form of a male horse, beheld his beloved wife once again, who was dark-complexioned and had assumed the form of a mare.
By the mere scent of their nostrils, two sons were born into that lineage; they were handsome, with beautiful limbs, and became physicians for the inhabitants of heaven.
And there Chāyā gave birth to a pair, O best of the twice-born: Tāpī and Śanaiścara, who causes all the worlds to suffer heat.
When the new moon indeed occurs during the conjunction of Saturn, it grants all desires; at that time, one should perform ritual bathing, charity, and the ancestral Śrāddha rite. || 51 ||
For such a man, prosperity is always in his grasp on this earth; having bathed at the confluence and given gifts according to his ability, he becomes purified. (52)
By worshipping Sthāvareśa, the destruction of one's sins occurs. Sauri, Śanaiścara, Manda, Kṛṣṇa, Ananta, Antaka, and Yama [are his names]. || 53 ||
Piṅga, Chāyāsuta, Babhru, Sthāvara, and Pippalāyana—these are the names of Śani; a person should recite them at the time of dawn.
For him, there shall never be affliction from Saturn; and even Yama-dharma performed penance here that was most difficult to endure.
In the northern part of the sacrificial pit, where the son of the Wind-god stands, there is that most excellent holy site (tīrtha) renowned by the name Dharmasaras.
Having bathed in that tīrtha where the son of the Wind-god attained supreme perfection through austerity, a man should indeed give a vessel of white copper.
Having respectfully adorned it with pearls, gems, and excellent golden ornaments, he gave that superior dwelling to Brāhmaṇas who were learned in the Vedas.
Having completely crossed over the world of the Mothers, that man who, on the eleventh day of both fortnights in the month of Śrāvaṇa, is honored in the world of Brahmā.
For one who always practices right conduct at the ford of Dharma and constantly performs rites such as bathing and giving gifts, the eternal world of Viṣṇu is attained.
Having bathed in Cyavanāśrama, a person should behold Cyavaneśvara, where the two meritorious Aśvins, the best of physicians, attained perfection.
By the grace of Cyavana, they both attained a place in the row of the gods; indeed, in former times, Cyavana himself obtained his sight through the divine physician.
O best of the twice-born, at that sacred ford a man shall possess divine vision; it was right here that the Sun attained the supreme hermitage of Agnihotra.
Following Sūryā, the highly fortunate Sāvitrī, who is world-renowned, she reached the realm of the Sun and enjoyed immense splendor.
Therefore, O Vyāsa, that supreme holy ford known as Kṣātā-saṅgama is meritorious, it removes all sins, and it bestows the boon of all desires. (65)
Listen now to the fruit of merit for him who, having risen in the morning, either hears this meritorious tale with devotion on earth or recites it. (66)
The fruit that is obtained on a festival day by [giving] a thousand tawny cows, one attains that same fruit; there is no need for deliberation on this matter. 67.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, I shall hereafter describe a certain holy place, the most excellent of all holy places, known by the name of Gayā. || 1 ||
Having bathed there regularly, a person is liberated from the three debts; having duly worshipped the gods and the ancestors, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
Vyāsa said: Among the Kīkaṭas, Gayā is meritorious; the river Punar-punā is meritorious; Cyavana’s hermitage is meritorious, and likewise Rājagiri is meritorious.
How was he known in the auspicious region of Mahākālavana? O ascetic, I wish to know this in detail.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, to this meritorious, purifying, and sin-removing narrative, by the mere hearing of which the ancestors attain the state of ultimate bliss. (5)
In ancient times, during the meritorious Kṛta Yuga, there was a king named Yugādideva; he was righteous in soul, and his name was auspicious to hear and to glorify.
As he protected his subjects properly, like his own biological sons, they became endowed with all prosperity and increased on all sides.
While that king rules, Dharma, consisting of four quarters, is eternal; the rain-cloud pours at the proper time, and the seasons follow their own courses.
The earth abounds with grain and fruit, and the cows yield much milk; the Brahmins are devoted to the recitation of the Vedas, and the Kṣatriyas are possessed of mighty arms.
The Vaiśyas were always devoted to wealth, and the Śūdras were intent on service; all were devoted to their respective castes and stages of life, and all were instructors of dharma. || 10 ||
Dharma, centered on the Śruti and Smṛti, brought joy and nourishment to the people; not a single human being was seen to be overcome by mental anguish or physical disease. || 11 ||
A woman who is immoral, unfortunate, or a widow is not even noticed; whether she has many sons, few sons, or dead sons, she is never considered barren. (12)
Endowed with beauty, virtue, and good qualities, she was devoted to her husband; nor was the path crowded with thorns or defiled by the presence of robbers. (13)

"Let there be constant offerings, let there be eating, and let there be giving in every house; may people be devoted to the practices of compassion, charity, austerity, fire-offerings, recitation, and sacrifice. (14)
People were seen everywhere devoted to all righteous duties; for Dharma moved on four feet, while Adharma was bodiless.
Thus was that righteous king, known as the Primordial God of the Age (Yugādideva), by whom this earth was protected and the subjects were made to flourish through dharma. || 16 ||
O Vyāsa, in ancient times, he performed ten million sacrifices in Avantī; at that time, there was an exceedingly powerful Dānava named Tuhaṇḍa.
By him this entire world, both moving and unmoving, was brought under his control; having performed fierce and meritorious penance, that wicked one obtained a boon from Brahmā.
Neither gods nor sacrifices existed, as they were abandoned by the path of the Vedas; there was no worship of deities, and neither the *svadhā* nor the *svāhā* was seen. (19)
O best of the twice-born, this eternal path of dharma has been uprooted by that evil-souled one; by him, all the gods have been rendered as good as destroyed.
Together with their fathers and the virtuous ones, they went to Brahmā for refuge, saying: "What shall we do, or where shall we go, having been utterly defeated by Tuhaṇḍa? (21)
Having heard these words of theirs, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, rose up and then went with them all to the realm of Viṣṇu.
Having gone there and propitiated Viṣṇu along with the hosts of gods, he offered praise to Viṣṇu of incomparable splendor by means of the Puruṣasūkta.
Indeed, all of them performed these rites for their own prosperity; then, desiring their welfare, an incorporeal voice spoke to them.
Listen, O best of gods, for that which is the highest welfare for you: go quickly to the Mahākāla forest on earth.
More secret than the secret, meritorious, purifying, and destructive of sin, it is that place where the illusion of deceivers does not manifest upon the earth. (26)
This sacred ford consists of all holy fords and bestows the boon of ten million fords; there flows the Śiprā, the most excellent of rivers, which grants the fruit of all desires.
The divine Mahākālī, the destroyer of the Daityas and the sovereign of the Kula, is surrounded by millions upon millions of attendants and is the increaser of the power of the Mothers (Mātṛs).
There is Gayā, which is greatly meritorious, as well as the great river Phalgu; there is the most excellent mountain Puruṣottama, and where Buddhagayā is remembered.
In that very way, Gayā is renowned today, famous throughout the three worlds; there is the sacred site of Viṣṇu’s sixteen steps, fashioned by Gadādhara.
Where the Prācī Sarasvatī, the merit-bestowing destroyer of all sins, flows; where the great river of the Asuras, said to be the giver of merit, is situated.
The Nyagrodha tree was declared by the great seer of old to be imperishable and eternal; it is there that the auspicious stone, which grants liberation to the departed spirits, is said to be located.
In that very place abide all those deities born from the lineage of the Pitṛs; Oṃkāra consists of all syllables, and Hari consists of all gods.
"The gods consist of all sacred fords (tīrtha), yet Gayātīrtha is unsurpassed; go quickly to that very place, and you shall attain supreme perfection."
Merely by entering there, all the ancestors dwelling in hell go to heaven and become fit for union with Brahman.
Vyāsa said: This most excellent and wonderful account of the majesty of Gayā has been narrated by you, O Blessed One; for everything is known to you, who possess the form of the universe.
O best of the twice-born, O ascetic rich in penance, I desire to hear all of that in detail: the supreme fruit of the śrāddha and [the merit] of the sacred field.
How many ancestors go eternally to the abode of the gods, satisfied? O sinless one, who are said to be the ancestors of whom, and for what purpose were they intended in ancient times? (3)
Sanatkumāra said: "You are blessed and you have fulfilled your purpose, since your mind is fixed upon the ultimate goal; nevertheless, O dear child, listen to the supreme procedure for the Śrāddha."
The worlds are established in the Śrāddha; in the Śrāddha, Dharma is firmly rooted. Indeed, the sacrifices that bestow the fruits of all actions abide in the Śrāddha.
Whatever is given with faith for the sake of the gods, for Brahman, or for the libation to the fire—one should know that to be a Śrāddha, as was declared of old by the Great Seer.
All humans, sages, gods, perfected beings (siddhas), and rākṣasas; gandharvas, kiṃnaras, nāgas, Brahmā, Īśāna, and the lords of the asuras. || 7 ||
Intent on their practice, they should offer the śrāddha rite intended for the three ancestors; thus, O Vyāsa, they obtain all desires whatsoever that reside in their minds.
Thus they continue this eternal, traditional path; nevertheless, these ancestors are indeed most highly renowned upon the earth.
I shall explain all of that exactly as it was heard; listen accordingly. These very ancestors are gods, and the gods are likewise ancestors. (10)
"O best of the twice-born, these ancestors and gods together were once asked this very question by Mārkaṇḍeya. (11)
Listen with a concentrated mind to all my thought as it is spoken: as many as those hosts of ancestors who have gone to that world.
Sanatkumāra said: These seven, the best among those who sacrifice, are all remembered as the hosts of Pitṛs; four of them indeed possess form, while three of them are formless.
I shall proclaim their worlds and their emanations; listen to that, O ascetic, as I describe their power and greatness in detail.
I shall proclaim the names and the worlds of those who have attained supreme austerity and who bear the very form of Dharma; listen to that.
The worlds known as Sanātanas exist there, radiant and formless; those hosts of Pitṛs are indeed the sons of Prajāpati.
O best of the twice-born, we have heard that the sons of Virāja are called Vairājas; the hosts of gods worship them with rites prescribed by the rules.
These very ones, having fallen from yoga, reach eternal worlds; then, at the end of a thousand yugas, they are born again as exponents of the Veda.
Having regained that supreme memory of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, those perfected ones attain the goal of Yoga, from which return is difficult to obtain.
O dear one, these are the ancestors of the yogins who increase their yoga; they are indeed those who, by the power of yoga, first nourish the moon.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, offerings should be given to the yogins with faith; this indeed is the foremost, unsurpassed ritual for the Soma-drinkers. (21)
The mental daughter of these [mountains] was named Menā, the excellent wife of Himavat, the great mountain, from whom Maināka is said to have been born. (22)
The illustrious great mountain named Krauñca is the son of Maināka; there dwell the radiant groups of ancestors known as the Agniṣvātta Pitṛs.
The Barhiṣads went to the southern quarter, the Yamās to the western direction, and the Somapās reached the northern direction protected by the Giver of Wealth (Kubera). || 24 ||
Kavyavāḍ and Anala are formless in the sky and on the earth. || 25 ||
The Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Piśācas worship those of purified soul; the Sādhyas worship the gods, and the Viśvedevas likewise worship the Ṛṣis.
Mānavas [worship] Śrāddhadeva, and the sages [worship] the eternal Brahman; thus the eternal dharma of Śrāddha has been handed down through tradition. (27)
The duty toward the ancestors is distinguished as superior to the duty toward the gods. The seven sons of Bharadvāja were entirely devoted to the dharma of the śrāddha.

Having attained the recollection of their past births, they have reached the state of Nirvana; whereas these seven lowest of the twice-born, having killed the milch-cow of their preceptor, [have fallen]. (29)
Intent upon their ancestors and tormented by hunger, they all ate; by the power of that merit, though fallen from yoga, they went to heaven.
Indeed, those seven became endowed with the memory of their past births and were united with yoga; therefore, the śrāddha has been declared as supreme by the wise, the knowers of the Supreme Self.
The worlds are established in the Śrāddha; in the Śrāddha is the supreme Yoga, O scorcher of foes! Thus have your ancestors been described; now hear the ritual procedure for the Śrāddha.
Delighting in celibacy, self-controlled, neither angry nor envious, devoted to purity and right conduct, steadfast, possessing insight into the scriptures, and having conquered his senses; || 33 ||
Thus, O Vyāsa, for one who performs a śrāddha, especially at a sacred ford (tīrtha), the satisfaction [of the ancestors] on the anniversary of death (kṣayāha) is said to be even greater than that.
Likewise, it is said that at a Vṛddhi-śrāddha there is [merit], and at a Mahālaya it is more than a hundredfold; O best of the twice-born, it is said to be ten times greater than that at Prayāga.
O best of men, the satisfaction at Kurukṣetra is ten times that of Prayāga; and from Kurukṣetra, O Vyāsa, Gayā is remembered as being ten times superior.
O Vyāsa, there are ten more [tirthas] in the auspicious Mahākālavana; in Avantī, it is meritorious in every respect, and Gayātīrtha is always [meritorious]. || 37 ||
For those whose ancestors have fallen into hell birth after birth, this extremely rare holy place exists for the sake of their liberation.
By the mere act of remembering [this] once, what is given becomes inexhaustible for the ancestors—even for those men who stand in the midst of battle and are deprived of their paternal lineage. (39)
Those who died in miscarriage, as well as those who have fallen away from their name and lineage—whether in one's own lineage or another's lineage—and others who died by suicide; ||| 40 ||
For the sake of their deliverance, let a śrāddha be performed there for those who died by hanging and those who died by means of poison or weapons.
For those who have died from the bites of fanged animals, or from physical deformities, or due to the loss of Brahmanical status—this Śrāddha is prescribed here for the sake of their deliverance.
Those living beings who have been consumed by fire, as well as others who have not been consumed by fire; || 43 ||
For the sake of rescuing those who have been struck by lightning or others who have been beaten with mallets, the śrāddha rite is prescribed here.
Those who have gone to Raurava, Andhatāmisra, and Kālasūtra, and those who have gone to the world of pretas, situated amidst manifold torments; || 45 ||

For the sake of the liberation of those who have gone to the terrible Asipatravana and Kumbhīpāka hells, as well as those born in animal wombs—birds, insects, and reptiles—a Śrāddha is prescribed here.
And those who have died in water, as well as women who have died during childbirth; || 47 ||
For the sake of the deliverance of those killed by horses, dogs, worms, fanged beasts, horned animals, or crushed by carts, the Śrāddha ceremony is prescribed here.

And for those who have been killed by weapons and missiles, by tigers, snakes, elephants, and kings, or by locusts, scorpions, fanged creatures, and thieves—even those whose fangs were broken—this Śrāddha is prescribed here for the sake of their deliverance. (49)

For those who died from the eight types of arrows (or fatal shafts), those devoid of purity and proper conduct, those who died of cholera, and those who died of dysentery—for their deliverance, the Śrāddha rite is prescribed here.

For those seized by *śākini* and other malevolent spirits, those who died in the midst of water, those touched by the touch of the untouchable, the sinful, and those deprived of offspring—for their deliverance, the *śrāddha* is prescribed here. (51)
"May the Śrāddha rite be performed for those who wander through thousands of other births by their own karma, for whom a human birth is so difficult to obtain. (52)

Those who were non-relatives in another birth, those who were relatives in another birth, those who were connected in another birth—whether friends, enemies, or others—for the sake of their deliverance, the Śrāddha is prescribed here. (53)

For the sake of the liberation of those who have died in the paternal lineage, as well as those in the maternal lineage, and those other kinsmen of the preceptor, the father-in-law, and relatives who have passed away—for their deliverance, the Śrāddha is prescribed here. (54)
For those in my family whose ancestral offerings have been interrupted, who are deprived of sons, wives, and so forth, and who have failed in their religious rites—for them this śrāddha is ordained.
The Śrāddha is ordained for those who were lame, hunchbacked, or deformed; for those who died as miscarriages; and for those in the family, whether known or unknown. (56)
And for those who have died by other forms of miserable death anywhere from the world of Brahmā downwards, this Śrāddha is prescribed here for the sake of their deliverance. (57)

For the sake of the deliverance of those who have died afflicted by thirst, hunger, or even abandoned [by others], as well as those who have entered the womb of a preta or the womb of a mleccha, the śrāddha rite is prescribed here.

O Vyāsa, one should perform the rite of ancestral offerings (śrāddha) at that sacred site in this manner; thus liberated from the three debts, he shall obtain his desired object. And having arrived at Gayā, all the gods, led by Indra, performed everything according to the rules as it was declared in the language of the gods.
Sanatkumāra said: Then all the hosts of gods, their sins shaken off and composed in mind, regained their former yogic power and returned to their respective offices as of old.
Thus, O Vyāsa, the sacred site of Gayātīrtha on the Kumudvatī is well-established; as are all the other holy fords and meritorious shrines within Gayā.

By bathing in those various holy fords (tīrthas), a person shall obtain the specific fruit of each respective ford; likewise, the sacred field of Gayā bestows the fruit of performing a śrāddha at Gayā.
And Phalgu, the best of rivers, likewise bestowing fruit; Ādigayā, Buddhagayā, and Viṣṇupadī are so remembered.
Likewise, Gayākoṣṭha has been proclaimed, as well as the footprints of Gadādhara; the sixteenth altar has been declared, and likewise the imperishable banyan tree.
The stone is likewise said to be the eternal granter of liberation from the state of a preta; it is called the river Acchodā and the supreme hermitage of the ancestors.
It is likewise the supreme hermitage for all the gods, dānavas, yakṣas, kinnaras, rākṣasas, and pannagas.

In all these places, rites such as bathing and giving gifts, as well as the ancestral śrāddha ceremony, should be performed according to the rules; thus one obtains the fruit of each respective sacred ford (tīrtha).
At Gayā, Janārdana himself exists in the form of the ancestors; by meditating upon that lotus-eyed one, one is liberated from the three debts.
Thus, O Vyāsa, the holy site of Gayātīrtha was originally established in Avantī; later, however, it appeared in Kaikaṭa, where the Asura resided.
O best of the twice-born, from that time onwards Gayā became established there; the great asura was struck down by the blows of Gadādhara’s feet.
And in that state, there is the majesty offered to Janārdana.

The sacred field of Gayā extends for five krośas, and Gayāśiras for one krośa; wherever I may perform it, what is given to the ancestors shall be inexhaustible. The Gayā-śrāddha is ordained to be performed at all times and on every occasion.

O Vyāsa, throughout the year, there is one supreme day established: when the Lord of Day (the Sun) is situated in Virgo and conjoined with the lunar mansion Hasta. That is called Mahālaya; what is given to the ancestors on that day becomes inexhaustible.
The Gayā-śrāddha is prescribed for all times and at all seasons. || 15 ||
O Vyāsa, once a year on this supreme day, people perform the most excellent Śrāddha for their mothers during the Anvaṣṭakā ceremony. || 16 ||
In this way, O Vyāsa, inexhaustible satisfaction arises for the ancestors for the duration of a kalpa through acts such as bathing and giving gifts in that beautiful city. || 17 ||
Furthermore, I shall fully proclaim its most wonderful majesty; listen to that which is being declared by me, which is purifying and destructive of sins. (18)
And the wives of the seven sages—the ṛṣipatnyas, devoted to their husbands—were corrupted by Svāhā and defiled by the fire.
Abandoned by the sages, they wandered from forest to forest; thus, after a long period of time had passed, Nārada, who has the vision of the gods, [appeared].
Seeking what was pleasing to them, he arrived within the forest; honored by them and firm in his vows, he remained seated there constantly.
He spoke with gentle words, speech appropriate to the place and time: "What is this strange occurrence? Why has this defeat of yours come to pass? (22)
And for what reason were the mothers of the world, devoted to their husbands, abandoned by the sages? (23)
The wives of the sages said: "O dear one, we do not know by what fault we were swiftly abandoned by the ascetics who maintain the sacred fires, on account of Kārttikeya. (24)
"Whatever lowly thing has arisen here by the power of fate, born from public scandal—what can we do, where shall we go, what austerity is there, and which deity [can help]? (25)
O Brahmin, having ascertained this, please speak according to the truth of the Vedas regarding that by whose merit of propitiation women may obtain the presence of their husbands.
Thus questioned then by those wives of the sages, Nārada, after meditating for a very long time, spoke for the sake of their welfare.
Nārada said: Listen, O best of ascetics, to the cause regarding you all: in the delightful Mahākālavana is the unsurpassed Gayātīrtha. (28)
Right there is the banyan tree named Akṣaya, the best among trees; by merely arriving there, you shall have shaken off all faults.
Go there without delay to that meritorious holy site, which removes all defects, grants the boons of all desires, and bestows every happiness.
O Vyāsa, having heard the words of Nārada and being well-urged by him, the wives of the sages desired their own beloved [husband] in the Mahākālavana forest.
They went to that forest where the sacred site named Gayā is located; having gone there and purified themselves, they performed the rites of bathing, giving gifts, and so forth.
And by those meritorious women, on the fifth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Nabhas, known as Ṛṣi-pañcamī, that well-performed vow was completed.
Having fasted for one night and kept a vigil through yoga, O Vyāsa, as soon as the vow was performed, they were instantly cleansed of their sins.

O best of sages, having been cast out due to their husbands' anger, they immediately attained the householder's stage of life (gṛhāśrama), which was bestowed by the sages along with the sacred fires as before.
From that time forward in this world, the fifth [lunar day] has been designated as the "Rishi-pañcamī. Whatever men or women perform devotion to it, [they shall attain the fruit]. || 36 ||

Having made wild rice their food, becoming pure and composed in mind, no misfortune or suffering whatsoever shall ever arise for them; nor shall women suffer from ill fortune or separation from their mothers.
"Whether through a son or through wealth, this will perhaps come to pass. Thus, O Vyāsa, has that which was asked by you been fully explained. (39)
O best of beings, such a holy place exists on earth in Avanti; there is nothing else that bestows such merit within the entire sphere of the universe.
If any man should perform great acts of charity at this sacred ford, his merits become inexhaustible, and he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
O Vyāsa, whoever, having become observant of the rules of restraint, listens to this discourse or constantly recites it, shall obtain the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Gayā-tīrtha," in the Avantī-kṣetra-māhātmya of the fifth section (Āvantya-khaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

Vyāsa said: O sinless one, you have previously mentioned Puruṣottama as the supreme sacred site (tīrtha). O Lord, tell me in detail the majesty of that sacred site; O best among the knowers of Brahman, I desire to hear this from you.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O best of the twice-born, to this supreme narrative that destroys all sins.
O Brahmin, by the mere hearing of which the destruction of great sins occurs, [it was told] in former kalpas in the pure and auspicious Vaikuṇṭha.
The Lord of Ramā was seated together with his attendants, Sanaka and the others, as well as the great sages of virtuous conduct led by Brahmā.

He was being served from all sides by those principles beginning with Mahat, endowed with the qualities of the eightfold supernatural powers (ṛddhisiddhi), as well as by hosts of Gaṇas and Gandharvas.
In courtyards made delightful by the emergence of wish-fulfilling gem palaces, amidst the honored songs of kinnaras and the dancing throngs of apsarases; || 6 ||
Seated indeed under the shade provided by a wish-fulfilling tree, all those enemies of Mura were devoted to the discourse on Dharma and firmly resolved upon the path of Brahman.
Among them, one supreme voice indeed questioned the Lord of Kamalā.
Lakṣmī said: "O Lord, I desire to hear the rule for meritorious acts in its true essence. You are omniscient and possessed of great wisdom; please speak of it, if it pleases you. (9)

The Blessed Lord said: "O beautiful one, charity, ritual bathing, austerity, and ancestral rites are indeed always praised; nevertheless, when performed according to the prescribed rule, all of that becomes inexhaustible. (10)

Giving, bathing, austerity, and ancestral rites performed by sages are said to be especially meritorious when conducted in a sacred place, at the right time, on a festival day, at a holy ford, in a temple, or at a sacred site.

On the full moon day, the new moon day, at the sun's passage into a new zodiac sign, during an eclipse, as well as on the days of Vaidhṛti and Vyatīpāta, the increase of the merit of giving is traditionally held to be supreme.
At the Gaṅgā, at Bhāskarakṣetra, at Kurukṣetra and Puṣkara, at the Godāvarī, at Gayā, and at the holy site of Amarakaṇṭaka—13.
Whatever is offered in sacrifice or given as a gift in Avanti becomes entirely inexhaustible; therefore, with every effort, one should visit a sacred ford on a festival day.
A man certainly becomes one who wears tattered rags, unfortunate, foolish, dull-witted, afflicted by disease, and fallen away from sacred fords and festivals. (15)
And what are the methods by which meritorious deeds should especially be performed? || 16 ||

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O sinless beloved, you have asked an excellent question regarding meritorious deeds. O beautiful one, those men who remain devoid of vows when the intercalary month (malamāsa) arrives, shall suffer from poverty birth after birth.
Śrī Rukmiṇī said: Of what nature is this impure month, and by what conjunction does it arise? At what time does it occur? Tell us this in detail. (18)

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Goddess, what you have spoken is appropriate; such a question is indeed timely. For the rites for the deities and ancestors must be performed according to the prescribed rule during the intercalary month (malimluca).
Shaving, the investiture of the sacred thread, marriage, as well as vows and fasts—these are especially to be avoided by householders by the best of eminent sages. (20)
And at the end of three years, this month arrives; because the sun does not transit [into the next sign] during it, it is therefore called the *adhikamāsaka* (intercalary month).
I am the presiding deity of the intercalary month and the eternal Supreme Person; my name and my auspicious sacred ford are located in the Mahākālavana forest.
My abode, known as Puruṣottama, is eternally established here; therefore, you must certainly go there with all possible effort along with me.
O beloved, in that Mahākālavana where there is the sacred ford named after me, living beings certainly come to bathe.
For them, there shall never be anything here that cannot be obtained from me; indeed, wealth, grain, wives, and the like, as well as the happiness of sons, shall always be theirs. (25)
Even when [the month] has not yet passed but has arrived, one should observe a vow dedicated to me; for I am always the lord of the intercalary month, O Puruṣottama.
Those best of men who perform bathing, giving, recitation, fire-offerings, Vedic study, libations to the ancestors, and worship of the deities at midday; || 27 ||
O Goddess, for those by whom the intercalary month has been passed in vain through negligence, all that [merit] of theirs shall certainly become inexhaustible in the lotus [of the heart]. (28)
Poverty always increases their grief and disease; when the intercalary month arrives, one should observe a vow in Avantī.

I shall give them to you out of affection, and to you alone—of this there is no doubt. Even a very small gift, whatever little has been performed here, shall all indeed become infinite through my grace, O lady of lovely appearance.
Śrī said: "O observer of noble vows, such indeed has been described by you regarding the intercalary month."
Indeed, even the greatness of the worlds bestows all desired boons; please, out of your grace, tell me of the meritorious vow of the intercalary month.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O beloved, when a month is obtained by men that lacks a saṃkrānti, then a great festival should be performed by those desiring their own welfare.
O Goddess of the Suras, on the fourteenth, the ninth, or the eighth day of the dark fortnight, this vow that destroys sorrow should be performed.
With whatever offerings are available, even during an intercalary month, having risen early on an auspicious day and performed the morning rites; || 35 ||
Having subsequently undertaken the vow while remembering Vāsudeva in his heart, O proud lady, [one should observe] fasting, eating only at night, or eating a single meal.
Having made this resolution for one [day], he should then invite Brahmins who are accompanied by their wives, of good conduct, of noble birth, and related by kinship.
Then, at the time of midday, one should have the eternal Lord, accompanied by Lakṣmī, installed in a flawless pitcher by the twice-born with Vedic mantras.
One should worship him, along with his ancestors and the lineage of ancestors, with supreme devotion; having established him with scented water and likewise with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
With nine kinds of sweet foods, as well as offerings of incense and lamps, with coverings and garments, and likewise with yellow silk cloths; || 40 ||
Accompanied by the sounds of bells and mṛdaṅga drums and the resonance of chanting, the observer of the vow should perform the ārārtika ceremony with camphor, agallochum, and sandalwood.

In the event that these are not available, one should offer even with firebrands for the sake of infinite fruit; [one should offer] into water contained in a copper vessel, along with sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and flowers.

Accompanied by his wife, with a joyful inner soul, he should offer the *arghya* after placing the two lotuses upon the ground together with the five jewels; taking them up with both hands, he should do so endowed with complete devotion.
The Arghya Mantra: O Compassionate One toward all beings, O Bringer of joy to the world! Accept this arghya, O Lord; be the bestower of complete fruit. 44.
The Prayer Mantra: Salutations to you, the Self-Existent One, to Brahmā of immeasurable splendor. Homage be to you, O Bliss of Śrī, O Bliss of Brahman, O Compassionate One! 45.
Having thus offered this prayer to Govinda, one should personally worship the Brāhmaṇas—who are pure, have bathed, and are accompanied by their wives—while recollecting Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. (46)
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rite, one should feed [the Brahmins] with ghee and milk-rice.
Having fed him according to the prescribed rite, as was appropriate for his wife, he who was endowed with learning and humility, together with his wife. (48)
Having worshipped according to one's ability with garments, ornaments, and saffron, as well as with cow’s milk, mangoes, wood-apples, dates, and plantains; || 49 ||
With jackfruits, coconuts, oranges, and pomegranates; with wheat cakes fried in ghee, auspicious *somālaka* fruits, and banyan figs.
With sweets filled with sugar and ghee, *karṇikas*, *khaṇḍamaṇḍakas*, vegetables of cucumber and *karkaṭī*, and ginger along with radishes; || 51 ||
And with various other vegetables and different kinds of ripe mangoes—specifically foods to be chewed, eaten, licked, and drunk, as well as tubers.
Having served the well-perfumed food and juices while speaking softly, he said: "This delicious, flavorful meal has been prepared for your sake. (53)
"O Lord, please accept whatever pleases you and whatever has been cooked by me; I am blessed, I am favored, and my home has been made meaningful. (54)
Then, having given betel leaves and sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), one should dismiss the Brahmins; for, O Goddess, betel leaf offered by four people gathered together is dear to me.
The man who gives [this] to the best of the twice-born shall become fortunate; and his wife shall always be well-behaved and ever beloved by her own kin.
O beloved, by means of betel-leaves one becomes endowed with the good fortune of sons; through the leaves Keśava is pleased, and through the areca-nuts the Lord (Īśa) together with Umā.
The Fire-god is pleased by incense powder, while the God of Love is pleased by the Khadira wood; that Viśvarūpa, who nourishes the three worlds, is pleased by all four. (58)
Having gratified those accompanied by their wives and having placed the sweetmeats (modakas) into their hands, he should follow them as far as the boundary and then eat together with his kinsmen.
O beloved, a woman who observes this vow here during the month of Aśvayuja shall never encounter poverty, grief for her sons, or widowhood.
Whether it be a man or a woman, whoever performs [this] during the intercalary month (malimluca) shall become an enjoyer of all happiness; of this there is no doubt at all.

How can those who, having encountered me, Nārāyaṇa, do not worship me here with supreme devotion, come to possess happiness, sons, wealth, friends, and a virtuous wife, endowed with all good qualities? (62)
Sanatkumāra said: Having encountered an intercalary month (adhimāsa), that foolish man who establishes his residence elsewhere—save for Mahākālavana—is a fool indeed. || 1 ||
O Vyāsa, when a man bathes in the sacred ford named Puruṣottama during an intercalary month and bestows gifts, his worlds shall be eternal.
Having worshipped Puruṣottama, whose feet are caressed by Ramā, one should likewise worship the goddess Umā together with Śaṅkara.

Having attained hundreds of desired objects, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. O Vyāsa, having fasted according to the rules on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada with a concentrated mind, one should perform a vigil at night.
One should perform the worship of Viṣṇu and likewise the water-procession at the lake of Puruṣottama constantly; hear now the meritorious fruit thereof. || 5 ||
Sons, wives, wealth, long life, health, and prosperity—for them, nothing whatsoever is difficult to obtain within the three worlds. (6)
In a region further to the east of that, on the bank where King Bhagīratha stayed, resides the great lord Jaṭeśvara as an ascetic.
Having performed austerities, that best among the meritorious attained supreme merit; indeed, he brought the Gaṅgā to the surface of the earth for the happiness of all the worlds.
Having bathed at its sacred ford, a man should cause a cow made of sesame seeds to be given as a gift; having obtained the fruit of all sacrifices, that man becomes possessed of sons.
In the northeastern part of that place, Rāma, the best of the Bhārgavas and a man of virtuous nature, performed austerities for the sake of purifying his own body.
And there is Kauśikī, the best of rivers, who bestows the excellence of all holy fords; having bathed there, a man is freed from the fault of killing a member of his own caste. || 11 ||
Upon beholding Rāmeśvara, a man shall be cleansed of all sin.

Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Bathing, Giving, and Other Rites during the Adhimāsa Month," within the "Greatness of Puruṣottameśvara" section of the "Greatness of the Avanti Region," in the fifth book (Āvantyakhaṇḍa) of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Vyāsa said: O Brahman, you have previously mentioned the eternal Gomatī-kuṇḍa; tell us in great detail at what time and when it was first established.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O highly wise one, to this supreme, merit-bestowing narrative that destroys sin—the account of the origin of Gomatīkuṇḍa as it was spoken of old by Rudra. (2)
And at Naimiṣa, the sages headed by Śaunaka were seated together, recounting the meritorious and auspicious narrative concerning the origin of all sacred fords (tīrthas).
On that auspicious occasion, the supreme majesty of Kāśī—purifying and destructive of sins—was narrated by Nārada himself.
Blessed is the city of Vārāṇasī, which is a saline field for both merit and sin; there, outcasts and scholars alike certainly attain liberation equally.
In the five-krośa region between the Asī and Varuṇā rivers, the fruit is great; even the gods desire death there—what need to mention other people? (6)
Having thus remembered, O Vyāsa, the Self-born One then replied while all the gods and sages were listening, O scorcher of foes.
There is no river equal to the Gomatī, no deity equal to Kṛṣṇa, and among all the netherworlds and the earth, there is no city equal to Dvārakā.
Having thus ascertained their resolve, all the sages, headed by Śaunaka, remained wherever they were in order to perform the morning twilight devotions.
There, on the very bank of the Gomatī, those who were firm in their vows performed [their rites]; Sāndīpani also performed his morning twilight devotions right there.
Thus, O Vyāsa, as he was practicing the vow of Sāndīpani, who resided in the city of Avantī, a great deal of time passed.
For the sake of fulfilling that very desire, Rāma and Janārdana, seekers of knowledge with delicate limbs and constant practitioners of celibacy, arrived there.
O scorcher of enemies, they took up residence in the house of that guru, who properly taught them all the supreme sciences and the entirety of the Vedas.
Day after day, he was seen in that very same place, yet the teacher was not there; "This is the time for instruction in the sciences—where has our excellent teacher gone? (14)
When they had thus questioned her, the preceptor’s wife replied: "O child, she always performs the morning twilight worship and other rites. (15)
Your guru indeed goes there daily for the purpose of bathing; the Gomatī is truly the best of rivers and the purifier in Dvārakā. (16)
Having heard this, Kṛṣṇa, joined then by Rāma, said: "What should be done here by us that would be for our own supreme benefit? (17)
"I long for the arrival of my guru right here, with the desire that he remain in this very place. At that very moment, Sāndīpani returned home.
Then, rising up, those two heroes, bowing with humility, offered salutations to their preceptor and spoke these words to him.
"Listen, O great yogin, to the reason for our stay: two seekers of knowledge have arrived here at your excellent home. (20)
"And it is morning time, O Brahmin; there is no leisure for us two, O Lord. Having heard these words of Kṛṣṇa and Bala, [the sage said: 21.
The blessed Vyāsa spoke regarding the reason for his own vow: "O child, this eternal vow is indeed considered our supreme practice."
The wise should always perform the Gomatī bath in the morning; it is certain that the meritorious worship of the Sandhyā should be performed right there.
"Having thus resolved, do whatever is appropriate for you to do. Hearing that, the Blessed Viṣṇu, possessing a form of illusory human nature, [acted].
O best of the twice-born, he performed the worship of Gomatī at Kuśasthalī, where the god Śiveśvara resides and where there is an unsurpassed sacrificial pit.
To the north of Kaṇṭheśvara, that Gomatī arrived; having pierced through the depths of Pātāla, she came together with the Sarasvatī.
Having risen in the morning, O Vyāsa, they all beheld Gomatī, the best of rivers, with her beautiful, long-cornered eyes, as she flowed toward their own hermitage.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Brāhmaṇa, the Gomatī, the best of rivers, has arrived right here; perform all rites such as bathing and giving gifts in this very place. 28.
The Sarasvatī merged here into the sacrificial pit along with the Gomatī; from that time forth, it has been called Gomatī-kuṇḍa in this world. (29)
The path to all the worlds is found right here; therefore, O Vyāsa, this is a most meritorious and unsurpassed sacred site (tīrtha) on earth. (30)
The Gomatī-kuṇḍa is proclaimed as the destroyer of all sins; on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhādra, it marks the occasion of Kṛṣṇa’s birth.
Having bathed there, a person should always perform a vigil at night; having fasted according to the rules, O Vyāsa, he should worship Vyāsa together with his disciples.
And he honored the excellent Vaiṣṇava men who were eager for the festival of Kṛṣṇa’s birth with various fragrant flowers and the like, together with garments and ornaments.
For those who, with concentrated minds, perform acts of worship toward cows and Brahmins, nothing whatsoever is difficult to attain in all the worlds.
From the merit born of bathing in the Gomatī and from the meeting with Vāsudeva, the attainment of the fruits of one's desires occurs; there is no doubt in this matter. (35)
Likewise, during the dark fortnight of Caitra, until it reaches the eleventh day, on that day a man should especially bathe in the Gomatī.
Having kept a vigil at night and likewise performed the worship of Viṣṇu, he then went to the Āmalakī tree and circumambulated it step by step.
Those who hear this meritorious, purifying, and sin-destroying narrative obtain the fruit of giving a thousand cows; of this there is no doubt. (38)
Freed from all sins, they go to the world of Viṣṇu. || 39 ||

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Gomatī-tīrtha Kuṇḍa," in the Avantī-kṣetra-māhātmya of the fifth section (Āvantya-khaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Sanatkumāra said: There is an unsurpassed holy site (tīrtha) there known as Kaṃthaḍeśvara. Having bathed in that holy site and beheld the Lord Maheśvara, a man [attains the highest goal]. || 1 ||
Pure and with a restrained mind, he is liberated from all sins; joined by hundreds of celestial chariots, he is glorified in the world of Śiva. || 2 ||
On earth, there is a supreme and most meritorious holy site that removes all sins, where the confluence of the Khagartā occurs in the vicinity of Gaṅgeśvara.
It removes great sins, is meritorious, and bestows the fruit of great merit; it is there that the Gaṅgā, the purifier of the three worlds, descended from the sky.
It was immediately placed upon his head by Mahādeva Śambhu; having bathed in that tīrtha, a person should behold Gaṅgeśa.
Having obtained the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu; having reached Vīreśvara, a man shall dwell in that sacred ford (tīrtha).
With his soul purified of all sins, he shall attain the world of heroes. There is another sacred ford of great merit, renowned on earth by the great seers.
Known as Vāmanakuṇḍa, it is renowned throughout the three worlds; by the mere sight of it, one is cleansed of the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Having attained a hundred desires, one shall thereafter go to the city of Viṣṇu. Vyāsa said: O sinless one, at what time did that which is called Vāmana arise in ancient times?
"I wish to hear all of that from you, O best among the knowers of Brahman. Sanatkumāra said: "Listen, O best of the twice-born, to this supreme narrative that removes all sins. (10)
Merely by hearing it, one is liberated from all sins; for in ancient times, the lord of the Daityas was declared to be solely devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu.
Renowned as Prahlāda, the best among all upholders of dharma, he surpassed Dharma in his conduct, and Ramā was surpassed by his truthfulness.
The worlds are sustained by his fortitude; the earth is supported by his forbearance; the divine oceans by his profundity; and hosts of enemies by his valor. (13)
Those who approached him with humility were conquered by that great-souled one; sacrifice was won over by his sacrificial fees, and the carrier of oblations (Agni) was won over by his offerings.

The Brahmins, whose souls were purified by cleanliness and right conduct, had their impurities destroyed by austerity; they were won over by gifts and honors, as well as by food, clothing, and other such provisions.
Birth is conquered by ritual refinement, and the eternal Self by self-restraint; the vital breath is conquered by breath-control, and Lord Hari by yoga and meditation. (16)
And such a great yogi, devoted to the true Dharma and steadfast like Prahlāda, has never existed before, nor will there ever be another.
His grandson was named Bali, who was ever devoted to righteous conduct; while he protected the subjects properly, they flourished exceedingly.
On this earth, there is no one who is short-lived, nor dull-witted, nor foolish, nor diseased, nor envious; nor is there anyone without a son or devoid of wealth. (19)
The great king Mahīpāla was a performer of sacrifices who bestowed abundant sacrificial fees; by him, the earth consisting of seven islands was always protected.
And once, while he was seated upon an excellent throne in the midst of the assembly, as shouts of "Victory! were being raised, the Gandharvas sang a charming song.
While musical instruments were being played, throngs of Apsaras danced as auspicious stories were being narrated by the learned.
O best of the twice-born, charioteers, panegyrists, perfected beings, bards, and highly learned sages all arrived at that very place.
Sunda, Upasunda, Tuhuṇḍa, and others, as well as the formidable Mahiṣāsura, the Dānavas Śumbha, Niśumbha, Dhūmrākṣa, and the Kālakeyas; || 24 ||
And the valiant Kālanemi, Daurhṛda, Mūṣaka, Yama, Nikumbha, Kumbha, Viśaṭha, and the exceedingly powerful Andhaka. || 25 ||
Śaṅkha, Jalandhara, Raudra, and the exceedingly powerful Vātāpi; Sarvajit, Viśvahaṃtṛ, Kāmacārī, and Halāyudha. || 26 ||
These and many others, the increasers of the Danu lineage, sat in attendance there upon the stainless King Bali.
Siddhas, Nāgas, Yakṣas, Kinnaras, and likewise Kiṃpuruṣas; those who move through the air and those who move upon the earth, as well as children and terrible Rākṣasas. || 28 ||
These and many other kings attended upon the monarch; and there, O best of the twice-born, that great celestial assembly hall shone with splendor.
Seated in that assembly hall, King Bali shone like the expanse of the sky in autumn, strewn with blazing planets.
Once, in the midst of the assembly, Nārada, who possesses divine vision, appeared like Vāsava surrounded by the Maruts and the gods in heaven.
When all those Dānavas had arrived and were standing there, seeing that he had come, all the sons of Diti rose up.
The king saluted that best of Kinnaras, Balin, in every way; having offered him a seat and shown him due respect, he inquired after his welfare.
Having performed the rites of hospitality and being seated, Nārada, the best of beings and foremost among sages, spoke to Bali with a voice as deep as a thundercloud.

Nārada said: Listen, O best of the sons of Diti; I went to the abode of Vṛṣabha. There was a beautiful, divine assembly of the gods, filled with celestial intentions. There, the gods along with the Gandharvas were gathered, led by Purandara.
Seated together, they were conversing with one another about meritorious matters; however, they could not endure the auspicious account of the Daityas related by Maya.
In ancient times, there was a Daitya named Hiraṇyakaśipu who was a lord of creatures; he was a conqueror of the three worlds and a leader by whom this earth was subdued.
Having brought the entire world under his control, he enjoyed the earth; he was exceedingly endowed with splendor and possessed great strength and prowess. || 38 ||
The self-controlled, all-pervading Kāmin was struck down by Nṛsiṃha; O Nārada, why do you praise Bali, whose strength in this world is so insignificant? (39)
Having thus insulted me, O best of Dānavas, Viḍaujas, the gatherer of the worlds, uttered many bitter words.
Therefore, O best of Dānavas, having conquered the earth inherited from your ancestors, obtain the status of a sovereign ruler of the whole world, O lord of the earth! (41)
"O best of Danujas, by what strength are the gods indeed sustained? They are ever intent on flight, subdued, and perpetually afraid of battle. (42)
"Having become devoted to my word, become the sovereign of the three worlds. Having heard these words of Nārada, Bali, the son of Virocana, then [acted].
O twice-born one, having consulted with all the asuras, the lord of all the daitya people conceived an incomparable wrath for the sake of conquering the three worlds. (44)
He waged a fierce battle with the mighty Vāsava; having conquered all the gods, he brought them, including Vāsava, under his control.
The asura Bali, son of Virocana, has become the lord of all the worlds; the gods have had their authority destroyed, they are defeated, and their kingdom is lost.
Behaving like mortals on earth, the hosts of gods, after waiting for some time, went to Brahmā for refuge.
"O Brahmin, O scorcher of foes, we have been cast down from the world of the gods by Bali; what shall we do, where shall we go, and whom shall we serve? (48)
Brahmā said: Listen, O best of gods, to your supreme means of accomplishment. Go, O most excellent immortals, to the beautiful city of Padmāvatī. 49.

Therein lies the most excellent and preeminent sacred ford (tīrtha), known by the name Uttaramānasa, where she is renowned as the bestower of the eight siddhis and the giver of great accomplishments to men.
O best of beings, the nine treasures (Nidhis) also reside there; on its southern side is the unsurpassed Viṣṇutīrtha.
Having bathed there, a person should behold Siddheśvarī, the bestower of perfect success; becoming intent upon prosperity and supernatural powers, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
Likewise, on the tenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina, one should worship Gaṇeśvara in the region of the Aṣṭasiddhi-śamī tree.
One who is established at the root of the Śamī tree shall be victorious in all worlds; there is no doubt about this. It eternally bestows prosperity, supernatural powers, and boons.
A person should indeed worship Gaṇeśa, the granter of all desires, constantly; having obtained the boon of all desires, he shall possess sons and wealth. || 55 ||
Therefore, with every effort one should go to Mahākālavana; go without delay to where the Viṣṇusaras tīrtha is located.
O best of gods, perform the worship of Viṣṇu, whose splendor is immeasurable; O foremost of deities, he shall be your protector from all fears.
Having heard these words of that Brahmā of purified soul, those gods, intent on accomplishing their task, arrived at Mahākālavana.
Having arrived here and purified themselves through acts such as bathing and giving gifts, the perfected ones (siddhas), devoted solely to devotion for Viṣṇu, sat down in worship.
Then all those gods, led by Śakra, respectfully asked Brahmā, the Creator, regarding the method for the worship of the Lord.
The gods said: "O Brahman, by what means does supreme devotion to Viṣṇu arise? O best among the knowers of Brahman, we desire to hear all that from you. (61)
Brahmā said: Listen, O best of gods, to this unsurpassed devotion to Viṣṇu: [one should meditate upon] the Lord who wears white garments, who is moon-colored, and who has four arms. (62)
One should meditate upon him with a serene countenance for the pacification of all obstacles. Blessed are they, victorious are they; whence could there be defeat for them? (63)
Those in whose hearts Janārdana—dark as a blue lotus—resides, and who is worshipped even by the gods for the sake of accomplishing their desired goals; || 64 ||
Salutations to that Lord of the Gaṇas, the remover of all obstacles; at the beginning of the Kalpa, I was impelled by Śauri, who desired to create.
Devoted solely to the meditation upon Viṣṇu, he was indeed unable to procreate. In the meantime, the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya suddenly appeared.

I saw one who was the lord of all accomplishments, self-controlled, long-lived, and a master of his senses; having gone there, I then approached him. Then, with eyes blossoming with joy, we both honored one another.
Then, while those two best of gods were seated comfortably and inquiring after my supreme well-being, I questioned that great sage Mārkaṇḍeya.
O Blessed One, by what means may my subjects be free from affliction? O Blessed One, saluted by sages, I desire to hear all of that. (69)
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Devotion to Viṣṇu is supreme and eternal; it destroys all afflictions and miseries, removes all sins, is meritorious, and bestows all happiness. (70)
This Brahma-great-lore (brāhmī mahāvidyā) must not be given to just anyone; it should not be given to one who is ungrateful, nor to one who is not a disciple, nor to an atheist, nor to a liar. 71.
To one who is envious, harsh, or lustful, that eternal Dharma which has entered into them will never at any time remove all obstacles.
This scripture is the most secret of all, the destroyer of every sin; it is the purest among the pure and the sanctifier of those who purify. (73)
The Thousand Names of Viṣṇu are auspicious and generate devotion to Viṣṇu; they grant all perfections to men and bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 74 ||

Oṃ. Of this mantra of the *Śrī Viṣṇusahasranāmastotra*, Mārkaṇḍeya is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Viṣṇu is the deity (*devatā*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chanda*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining all desires through recitation. Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): I bow to the young cowherd boy, who is dark blue like a water-laden cloud; whose noble character has been revealed; who holds a mountain in the palm of his hand; who delights in playing the flute; who protects the community of Vraja; who is intent on the amorous play with the lovely women; and who wears a garland of fresh *tulasī*. (75)
Oṃ! Viṣṇu is the universe, the lord of the senses, the self of all, the creator of all; he is omnipresent, the lord of the night, and the abode and non-abode of the multitude of beings. (76)
The God is without beginning or end, omniscient, the source of all, all-pervading, the sustainer of the world, the possessor of all powers, and sinless.

The seed of the universe, the creator of the universe, the lord of the universe, the master of the universe; the teacher of the universe, the protector of the universe, the sustainer of the universe, and that which consists of the universe. (78)
Janārdana assumes every form and possesses every universal shape; he is unborn, eternal, constant, the support of the universe, all-pervading, and the Lord.
He is of many forms and yet of one form; Hara assumes all forms. He is the wind born from the fire of time, the inexhaustible bringer of the end of the dissolution.
The great ocean, the great cloud, the arising of water-bubbles; the conditioned, the transformed, the fish, the great fish, and the timiṅgila. || 81 ||
Ananta, Vāsuki, Śeṣa, Varāha the upholder of the earth, the swan enriched by the discrimination between water and milk, and the one residing on the Golden Mountain (Meru). 82.
Hayagrīva, Viśālākṣa, Hayakarṇa, Hayākṛti, Manthana, Ratnahārī, Kūrma, and Dharadharādhara. || 83 ||

He is free from sleep yet the sleeping one, the joyful one, the exceedingly joyful one, and he who is dear to Nandana; he is the navel-stalk and the lotus fiber, the self-born one, and the four-faced one.
Dakṣa is devoted to Prajāpati; he is the creator of emanation and the progenitor of offspring. Marīci, Kaśyapa, and Dakṣa are the teachers of gods and asuras, as is Kavi.
Vāmana, the follower of the left path, the performer of left-handed rites, the one of vast body; the traverser of the three worlds, the lamp, the destroyer of Bali’s sacrifice. || 86 ||

The destroyer of sacrifice, the performer of sacrifice, the Lord of sacrifice, the all-pervading enjoyer of sacrifice; the thousand-rayed one, Bhaga, Bhānu, Vivasvat, Ravi, and the radiant Aṃśumān. || 87 ||
Manu, the witness of karma, is both of fierce splendor and of little splendor; he is the king of the gods, the lord of the celestials, the enemy of the Dānavas, and the husband of Śacī. (88)

Agni is the friend of Vāyu and the bearer of oblations; Varuṇa is the lord of aquatic creatures; Nairṛta is the devourer and the one without beginning; and [Kubera] is the lord of the Rakṣasas, Yakṣas, and wealth. || 89 ||
Kubera is the possessor of wealth, Vego is the protector of riches, Vasupāla is the creator of splendor, Amṛtasravaṇa is Soma, Somapānakara is the wise one. || 90 ||
The source of all medicinal herbs, the glorious one, the moon and the sun, the enemy of poison, the remover of poison, and the mountain that bears the poison upon its neck.
The blue-throated one, the bull-bannered, Rudra, the moon-crested lord of Umā; Śiva, the peaceful, the self-controlled, the heroic, the meditator, the honorable, and the bestower of honor.
He is a worm, an insect, a hunter of deer, a slayer of deer, and one marked by the deer; he is a young student, Bhairava, a child, a skull-bearer, and one whose body is a staff.

Dwelling in cremation grounds, a consumer of flesh, a destroyer of the wicked, and the end-maker of the best; a yogi who terrifies the yoginīs, established in meditation, and whose very being is meditation.
The leader of the army, the giver of armies, Skanda, Mahākāla, the lord of the Gaṇas; the primordial god, the lord of the Gaṇas, the destroyer of obstacles, the annihilator of impediments. || 95 ||
The bestower of supernatural powers and perfection, Dantī, Bālacandra, Gajānana, Nṛsiṃha, Ugradaṃṣṭra, Nakhi, and the destroyer of the Dānavas. || 96 ||
The nourisher of Prahlāda, the lord of all the Daitya folk, Śalabha, Sāgara, the witness, and the fashioner of the Kalpas. || 97 ||
He is gold, the possessor of gold, the maker of snow, and the snowy mountain (Himācala). He is the upholder of the earth, the giver of land, Meru, Kailāsa-śikhara, and Giri. || 98 ||

He who illuminates the world and its beyond, the dweller within the worlds, the observer, the Lord of the universe, the guardian of the quarters, the lord of the directions, the divine one, possessed of a divine body, and the master of his senses. || 99 ||
Virūpa, Rūpavān, Rāgī, and one skilled in dance and song; Hāhā, Hūhū, Citraratha, and the divine sage Nārada as a friend. 100.
The Viśvedevas, the Sādhyadevas, Dhṛtāśī, Calo'cala, Kapila, Jalpaka, Vādī, Datta, and Haihayasaṃgharāj; (1)
Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Bhṛgu—the foremost of the seven ṛṣis—and the great hero Jamadagni, the ṛṣi who brought an end to the Kṣatriyas. || 2 ||
Hiraṇyakaśipu, Hiraṇyākṣa (the beloved of Hara), Agasti, Pulaha, Dakṣa, Paulastya, Rāvaṇa, and Ghaṭa. || 3 ||

The enemy of the gods, the ascetic, the scorcher, the beloved of Vibhīṣaṇa and Hari; the radiant one, the destroyer of radiance, the possessor of splendor, the Lord, the sovereign of kings, the Master. || 4 ||
Rāma, the descendant of Raghu and son of Daśaratha, the enhancer of the lineage of Raghu; the husband of Sītā, the glorious lord, devoted to Brahman, and affectionate toward his devotees. || 5 ||
He was armored, clad in mail, bearing a sword, dressed in rags or naked; he wore a crown and earrings, held a bow, and carried a conch, a discus, and a mace.
The noble son of Kausalyā, who sleeps upon the ground and is dear to Guha; the son of Sumitrā, Bharata the youth, and Śatrughna, the elder brother of Bharata.
Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy heroes; the lord of monkeys accompanied by his wife; Hanumān; and Sugrīva, the king of bears and the destroyer of Vālin. || 8 ||

He is fond of messengers and a performer of missions; he possesses limbs and is the best among those who speak; he is the destroyer of forests, the speed of the forest, he whose banner is a monkey, and he who has a tail.
Ravidaṃṣṭrin, Laṅkāha, Hāhākāra, Varaprada, Bhavasetu, Mahāsetu, Baddhasetu, and Rameśvara. (110)

The beloved of Jānakī, the lover, the wearer of the diadem, the wearer of earrings, the wielder of the sword; he whose eyes are as broad as lotuses, the long-armed one, whose form is like a rain-cloud. 11.

He is restless, fickle, full of desire, fond of women, and devoted to the left side of his body; he is dear to women, intent on women, dominated by women, and has women as the dwellers upon his left side.

He had conquered his enemies, conquered desire, and conquered anger; he had mastered his senses, was peaceful, self-controlled, delighted in compassion, and was uniquely devoted to the vow of celibacy.
He was composed of pure goodness, established in sattva, the destroyer of pride and anger, and firm; he was surrounded by many rākṣasas and was the destroyer of all rākṣasas.

He is the slayer of Rāvaṇa’s wife, the one who humbled Rāvaṇa in battle by cutting off his ten heads; he is the ruler of the kingdom, the performer of sacrifices, the giver, the enjoyer, and one whose wealth is asceticism.
The beloved lord of Ayodhyā, Vaikuṇṭha of unimpeded form, who is devoted to truth, observant of vows, heroic, an ascetic, and the bestower of the fruit of truth. || 16 ||
He is the witness of all, omnipresent, the destroyer of all life-breaths, and imperishable; he is Prāṇa, Apāna, Vyāna, Udāna, and Samāna.
Nāga, Kṛkala, Kūrma, Devadatta, and Dhanañjaya; he is the pervader who knows all vital breaths and sustains those who maintain yoga. || 18 ||

He is the knower of reality, the giver of reality, the possessor of reality, and one who is proficient in all principles; he is established in meditation, endowed with meditative power, high-minded, and the foremost among those who know yoga.

He is the knower of Brahman, the giver of Brahman, the knower of the knower of Brahman, and the source of Brahman; he is the lamp for those who know the supreme self, the embodiment of light, and the stainless one.

The Guru is the giver of knowledge, the destroyer of ignorance, and the wise instructor of disciples; the good disciple is one who is trained, well-behaved, and expert in the instruction of other disciples. || 21 ||

He is the mantra, the destroyer of mantras, the master of mantras, and the knower of tantras; he is dear to those born of the tantras, the true mantra, the knower of mantras, the master of mantras, and the sole shatterer of the spells of the yantras. || 22 ||

The slayer, the deluder, the deluded one, the wicked one who performs paralyzing and eradication, the one of many illusions, the illusion-less one, and the great illusionist who bewilders with his magic. || 23 ||

The giver of liberation and the binder, the prisoner, the attractor and the repeller; he who is the syllable *hrīṃ* in the form of a seed-syllable (*bīja*), and the syllable *klīṃ*, the lord of the *kīlaka*. || 24 ||

He is the utterance *sauṃ*, the possessor of power, the power itself, the bearer of all powers, and the sustainer; he is the syllables *a*, *u*, and *oṃ*, and he is born from the *chandogāyatra* meters.

The Veda, the knower of the Vedas, the knower of the Vedas, the student of the Vedas, Sadāśiva; the Lord of the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāman, and Atharva Vedas, the performer of Sāman chants, and the non-performer (of worldly acts). || 26 ||
He has three feet and many feet; he is the Śatapatha [Brahmana] with faces on all sides. He is the Prakrit, the Sanskrit, and the Yogin; he is the song, the book, and the riddle.

He is with qualities and devoid of qualities; He is the Vedic meter, unattached, devoid of qualities, yet possessed of qualities; He is without attributes, yet possesses attributes; He is associated with attachment, an agent, a follower of dharma, and the bestower of the fruits of action.
Free from ritual action, yet desiring desires; unattached and devoid of attachment; free from greed, free from egoism, and beloved by those who possess nothing. || 29 ||
He who forms attachments to everything yet is full of passion, who renounces everything yet wanders outward; he who has one foot, two feet, many feet, or few feet. (130)
He has two feet, three feet, no feet, or one foot; he is the collection of all steps. He moves through the sky, he moves upon the earth, he wanders, and he is as fond of honey as a bee or a worm.
He is the sacrifice, the year, the month, the calculated sun, and indeed day and night; he is the Kṛta, Tretā, Kali, and Dvāpara ages, possessing four forms.
Time is the maker of day; it is the eternal family dharma. It consists of kalās, kāṣṭhās, kalās, nāḍīs, yāmas, and the bright and dark fortnights.

He is the yoke, the sustainer of the yoke, the worthy one, the promoter of the law of the yoke; he is the conduct of the lineage, the maker of the lineage, the creator of the lineage's deity, and the noble-born.
He was a practitioner of the four stages of life: a householder indeed fond of guests, a forest-dweller wandering in the woods, and one who had fulfilled the stage of the forest-hermit (vānaprastha).

He was a young ascetic, a celibate student, wearing a topknot and sacred thread, carrying a water-pot, possessing three matted locks, absorbed in meditation, a meditator, and a resident of Badarikāśrama. (36)

Born from Hemādri, he is indeed Haima; he is a heap of gold, yet his form is that of a Makara. He is a Brahmin who has set out on the Great Journey, one who is both dispassionate and possessed of passion, and a householder.
Nara-Nārāyaṇa, free from sin, whose form is as noble as Kedāra; the essence of penance at Gaṅgādvāra, a treasure-trove of austerity in the forest of asceticism. || 38 ||
This is the treasure Mahāpadma, the abode of the splendor of the lotus-pond; he is Padmanābha, the all-pervading soul, the wandering mendicant, the Supreme Person.
He is supreme bliss, the ancient one, the sovereign emperor, the king who shines forth; he dwells in the wheel, he stands as the protector of the wheel, the universal monarch, the lord of men.
The physician is the knower of Ayurveda and Dhanvantari, the destroyer of disease; the patient is born from the seeds of medicinal herbs and is the one who effects the destruction of disease. (41)

He is consciousness, the conscious one, the inconceivable, the destroyer of mental thought; he is beyond the senses, the touch of bliss, the one who moves about, and the bird-like traveler through the heavens.
Garuḍa, the king of birds, the son of Vinatā born of Cakṣuṣa, who is mounted upon the celestial chariot that serves as Viṣṇu’s vehicle and possesses horses of mind-like speed.
The rain-giver who brings abundant showers, the one who causes Airāvaṇa to cry out; he who is Uccaiḥśravas, Aruṇa, Gāmī, Haridaśva, and Haripriya. 44.
Prāvṛṣa, Meghamālī, Gajaratna, Purandara, Vasuda, Vasudhāra, Nidrālu, and Pannagāśana; || 45 ||
He who reclines upon Śeṣa, who lies upon the waters, Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, the one who divided the Vedas, the eloquent speaker, and the arranger of many branches [of the scriptures].
