He is memory, the seeker of the meaning of the ancient dharma, and one who discerns the higher and the lower; he has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and shines with a thousand faces.
He who has a thousand arms, a thousand rays, and a thousand beams; the Man; he who has many heads and one head; he who has three heads and no head; the Glorious One.
He has matted hair and is smeared with ashes, yet he wears divine garments and is pure; he may be minute in form or vast in form, deformed or of extraordinary appearance.
Hari is the churner who churned the ocean and the taker of all jewels; he is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the one adorned with lapis lazuli, and the great wish-fulfilling gem.
Priceless, yet of great value; beyond price, fragrant, and blissful; father, mother, child, kinsman, creator, fashioner, noble lord, and restrainer. || 51 ||
Abiding within yet acting externally, staying outside yet moving abroad; the purifier, the fire, the cooker, the consumer of all, the eater of oblations.

The Blessed One, the destroyer of fortune, the possessor of fortune, the breaker of worldly existence, the terrifier; he who dwells in the body, the performer of action, the agent of what must be done, and the bestower of hands.
He who possesses one quality and two qualities; he who is happy; he who subsists by means of a messenger; the child; the savior; the protector; time; and the devourer of mice. (54)
The reviver, the maker of life, the living one, the source of life; the twenty-sixth, the Great Viṣṇu, the all-pervading Maheśvara. || 55 ||

He has divine limbs, wears a garland of pearls, bears the Śrīvatsa mark, and has the dolphin as his emblem; he is dark-bodied, as dark as a rain cloud, clad in yellow garments, and possesses a beautiful countenance.
Clad in bark garments and yet divested of clothing, beloved by spirits and dānavas; immortal and a partaker of immortality, he assumes the form of the enchantress Mohinī. || 57 ||
He possesses divine vision and impartial vision; he is the deceiver of gods and demons. He is Kabaṃdha, the maker of comets, Svarbhānu, and the scorcher of the moon.

The king of planets, the seizer, the grasper, the liberator from all planetary afflictions; he is the one who is favorable through gifts, honor, recitation, and fire-offerings, the auspicious planet. (59)

He is the creator of obstacles and the remover [of them], the destroyer of obstacles, and the leader (Vināyaka). He is both the doer of harm and the doer of favor, and the bestower of the fruits of all spiritual accomplishments (siddhi). || 160 ||

A servant, one who employs conciliation and gifts, one who sows dissension, one who uses force, and one who is envious; one who is compassionate, one whose nature is generosity, a donor, a performer of sacrifices, and a recipient of gifts. (61)

The oblation, the fire, the vessel for the caru-offering, the sacrificial fuel, the wind, Yama, the Hotṛ priest, the Udgātṛ priest, Śuci, the Kuṇḍa, the Sāmaga, Vaikṛti, and the Sava sacrifice; || 62 ||

The substance, the vessels, the resolve, the pestle, the two fire-sticks, the kuśa grass, the initiated one, the pavilion, the altar, the sacrificer, the sacrificial animal, and the sacrifice; || 63 ||
Dakṣiṇā, Svastimān, Svasti, Āśīrvāda, Śubhaprada, Ādivṛkṣa, Mahāvṛkṣa, Devavṛkṣa, and Vanaspati. || 64 ||
Prayāga, Veṇumān, Veṇī, Nyagrodha, the imperishable Vaṭa, Sutīrtha, Tīrthakārī, Tīrtharāja, Vratī, and Vrata. (65)

Pṛthu is the giver of livelihood, the son; the cow is the milker, and the calf likewise. He is the milk, the carrier of milk, the possessor of milk, and the knower of the light that shares in the portion of milk.

He is the knower of the portions of sovereignty, the possessor of all portions, the one who differentiates all portions; he is the vehicle, the rider, the swift, the pedestrian, and the practitioner of austerity.
The protector, the guardian, the cowherd, the one who sports with the cowherd girls; Vāsudeva, the large-eyed one, Kṛṣṇa, the beloved of the cowherd women. 68.
The delighter of Devakī, the Joyful One, the ascetic in the home of the cowherd Nanda; the son of Yaśodā, the Bondmaid, Dāmodara, and the one who dwells in the mortar.
The enemy of Pūtanā, the one who moves on his feet, the playful breaker of the cart, the lover of fresh butter, the eloquent one, and the boy who tended the calves. || 170 ||
He who assumes the form of a calf, the protector of calves, the slayer of calves, the ender of the demon Dhenuka; the enemy of Baka, the forest-dweller, and the one skilled in forest sports.
He is dark-complexioned and lovely in form, holding a flute and a staff; he is the liberator of the cowherds, liberation itself, and one who wanders upon the banks of the Yamunā.
The master of illusion, the illusory one, who deludes with the illusion of Brahmā; he who knows how to sport with his own essence, the child among the cowherd boys. || 73 ||

The one who wanders among the cattle, the lord of cattle, the cowherd, the mighty upholder of Govardhana; he who possesses the splendor of Indra, the destroyer of sacrifices, the stayer of rain, and the protector of the cows. || 74 ||
The provider of fragrant protection, the creator of the forest-draught in the Kali age, the subduer of Kālīya, and the one who sports in the pool of the Yamunā river; || 75 ||
Saṃkarṣaṇa, Baladeva, Halāyudha, Lāṅgalin, Musalin, Cakrin, Rāma, and Rohiṇinandana—these are the names by which he is praised for his strength.

The one who dragged and lifted the Yamunā; the one clad in blue garments; the wielder of the plow; the one who possesses a plow; the lover of Revatī; the restless one; and the supreme bestower of great honor.

The enemy of Dhenuka, the great hero, the one who sports with the cowherd girls; he who removes the pride of Kāma, the lover, whose dwelling is among the cowherd women, and who steals away their garments.
He is the player of the flute and the musician, skilled in dance and song; he is the singer who infatuates the cowherd girls, the leader of the rāsa dance, and the night-stalker.
He who wears divine garlands, he who is stainless, and he who is adorned with a forest garland; the enemy of Kaiṭabha, the enemy of Kaṃsa, the slayer of Madhu, and the subduer of Madhu.
The wrestler who crushed Cāṇūra, the destroyer of Muṣṭika with his fists, the slayer of Mura, the giver of joy, the one who intoxicates, the destroyer of pride, and the end-maker of Naraka. || 81 ||

He was a student of the sciences, a sleeper upon the ground, a giver of gifts, a good friend, and happy; he was whole yet seemingly incomplete, a physician, and indeed a treasury of the arts. || 82 ||
He is possessed of knowledge, he is vast, the liberator of his father and mother, the lover of Rukmiṇī, the delightful one, the lord of the Yamunā, and the wielder of the conch.
Pāñcajanya, Mahāpadma, the leader of many leaders, Dhundhumāra, the slayer of Nikumbha, the ender of Śambara, and the beloved of Rati. || 84 ||
Pradyumna and Aniruddha, Arjuna the lord of the Sātvatas, Phālguna, Guḍākeśa, Savyasācī, and Dhanañjaya. (85)
Kirīṭin, bow in hand and expert in the science of archery; Śikhaṇḍin, Sātyaki, Śaibya, and Bhīma of terrible prowess. || 86 ||
Pāñcāla and Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadrā and husband of Draupadī; Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Dharma, who is truthful and pure in his vows. (87)
Nakula and Sahadeva, Karṇa, and the compassionate Duryodhana; then Bhīṣma, the son of Gaṅgā and Bhagīrathī, with mace in hand. 88.
Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who possesses the eye of wisdom, Bhāradvāja, Gautama, Aśvatthāman, and Vikarṇa—all experts in battle—desisted.
Sīmantika, Gadī, Gālava, Viśvāmitra, Durāsada, Durvāsas, Durvinīta, and the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya. || 190 ||

Lomaśa (hairy), Nirmala (stainless), Alomī (hairless), Dīrghāyus (long-lived), Cira (lasting), Acirī (momentary), Punarjīvī (reborn), Mṛta-bhāvī (destined to die), Bhūta (past), Bhavya (present), and Bhaviṣyaka (future). || 91 ||

He who is the three times, the three genders, the three-eyed one, and the lord of the three steps; he who belongs to the Yadu clan, who is Yājñavalkya, and who causes the lineage of Yadu to flourish. || 92 ||

He who sports with arrows, he who sports victoriously, the destroyer of the Yādavas, the Kali age; he who is compassionate, the heart itself, the gift, the heir, the recipient of inheritance, and the possessor of fortune.
He is the great ocean and the surface of the earth; he makes his dwelling upon the Blue Mountain (Nīla-parvata); he is of a single color and yet devoid of color; he moves outside all colors.

The censurer of sacrifice, the censurer of the Vedas, the one outside the Vedas, the powerful, the mighty; the enemy of the Buddhists, the tormentor, the affliction; the Lord of the world, the Master of the universe. || 95 ||

He is devotion, the possessor of the portion of the Lord, the one who has divided [the world], and the beloved of the Blessed One; he is the triple village, the nine forests, and the seat of the secret Upaniṣads. || 96 ||
Śāligrāma, Śilāyukta, Viśāla, Gaṇḍakāśraya, Śrutadeva, Śruta, Śrāvī, Śrutabodha, and Śrutaśravas. || 97 ||
Kalki, the essence of time, the impurity that effects the destruction of wicked barbarians; he who is saffron-hued, white, steadfast, the creator of forgiveness, and the bull-leaping god.
Kiṃkara, Kinnara, Kaṇva, Kekī, and the lord of the Kiṃpuruṣas; Ekaroman, Viroman, Bahuroman, and Bṛhatkavi. || 99 ||

The wielder of the thunderbolt-weapon, the possessor of the vajra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the younger brother of Vāsava; he who possesses many sacred fords, the ford itself, and the lord of all those born at the sacred fords. || 200 ||

The Vyatīpāta yoga and the lunar eclipse are auspicious, bringing about an increase in the merit of giving; he is innumerable, immeasurable, the very form of number, yet beyond all calculation. || 1 ||
The dispeller of mist, the star, the young moon, and the nectar-maker—what is his color, what is he like, what does he do, what is his nature, and what is his support? || 2 ||

He is without light and without form, yet the single agent of manifold forms; he is the daughter’s son, the son’s son, the grandson, the great-grandson, the upholder of the lineage, and the sustainer.
Melted, compassionate, and the bestower of all accomplishments is the jewel. || 4 ||
The son of the Earth is the support and the sustainer; he is most auspicious, Mangala, whose form is auspicious, the source of all blessings, and the embodiment of every auspiciousness.
This is the thousand names of Viṣṇu, whose splendor is incomparable; it bestows all perfections, fulfills desires, is meritorious, and has Hari and Hara as its essence.
Whoever, having risen at dawn, being pure and composed, should recite this; and whoever, with a steady mind, should hear this daily—(7)
Endowed with faith, one who performs this at the three junctions of the day is liberated from all sins; honored by sons, grandsons, wives, and servants, he rejoices.
He attains vast fortune, is liberated from all distress, obtains all his desires, and gains extensive renown. || 9 ||
The learned Brahmin becomes possessed of knowledge; the Kṣatriya shall be victorious; the Vaiśya shall be enriched with the gain of wealth; and the Śūdra shall obtain happiness. || 210 ||
In a terrible battle, in a dispute, and in business dependent on others, he who is victorious shall always attain victory in all undertakings.
Whether reciting it once, ten times, a hundred times, or a thousand times, a man who recites it constantly indeed attains the corresponding fruit.
One desiring sons obtains sons; one desiring wealth obtains inexhaustible wealth; one desiring liberation obtains liberation; and one desiring dharma obtains an accumulation of dharma.

One seeking a daughter obtains a daughter, though she be difficult even for the gods to attain; one seeking knowledge becomes a man of knowledge, and a yogi is joined to the practices of yoga. || 14 ||
During terrible and great portents, in times of famine and royal conflict, when a great plague has arisen, and when one is afflicted by poverty and suffering. (15)
Whether in a forest or a wilderness, even when surrounded by a forest fire, or in a jungle overcome by lions and tigers and teeming with elephants; (16)
When commanded by an enraged king to engage in battle with bandits, or during terrible lightning strikes, this [mantra] should indeed always be remembered by men. (17)
Even during fierce afflictions by the planets, or when undergoing execution or imprisonment, and even for those on a boat in the great ocean or upon a mighty river, there shall be no calamities.
Those who are afflicted by disease, discolored, or deprived of hair, nails, and skin, become possessed of divine bodies through either reciting or hearing [this].
In the vicinity of a Tulasī grove, on an island in a lake, in a divine abode, in the auspicious region of Badarikāśrama, at Gaṅgādvāra, or in a forest of asceticism; || 220 ||
In Madhuvana, at Prayāga, in Dvārakā, and in Mahākālavana, those who are concentrated and self-restrained attain the fulfillment of all desires.
Those who, being devoted and having conquered their senses, recite this a hundred times, become perfected ones (siddhas) who bestow success upon the world and wander upon the surface of the earth.

It is the supreme means for establishing friendship among those who are divided by mutual enmity; it is the deluder of those who seek to delude others, and it is purifying and destructive of sin. (23)
It is the supreme means for pacifying the afflictions caused by child-seizing spirits, and it is the ultimate destroyer of the intellects of the wicked and the sinful. (24)

A woman who has a miscarriage, one who is barren, one who suffers from leakage during pregnancy, or one who gives birth only to female children, shall constantly give birth to a son without any effort. || 25 ||
Cows yield abundant milk; agriculture yields much grain and fruit; servants are devoted to the duty toward their master; and women become faithful to their husbands. (26)
For the destruction of untimely death, as well as upon seeing an evil dream, and in all rites for pacification, it should always be remembered by men. (27)
The mortal who, being pure, alone, having conquered his appetite, subdued his anger, and mastered his senses, recites this daily in the presence of Viṣṇu— || 28 ||
Endowed with the power of mounting Garuḍa, clad in yellow garments, and possessing four arms, he attains his desire in this world and goes to the realm of Viṣṇu.
On one side are all branches of knowledge, on the other all austerity; on one side is the entirety of dharma, and likewise on the other side is Viṣṇu.
For that twice-born man who desires to offer praise with the Thousand Names, he has indeed already offered praise with this single verse; of this there is no doubt. (31)
O thousand-eyed one, thousand-footed, blazing with a thousand faces, possessing a thousand names and infinite eyes, you who have a thousand arms—salutations be to you!
The Thousand Names of Viṣṇu, which is ancient and in accord with the Vedas, should always be recited by devotees; it is the most auspicious of all auspicious things. (33)
O twice-born one, when the gods were thus engaged in praise there, the Blessed One, the giver of boons who is worshipped by those who seek boons, spoke directly to them.
The Blessed Lord said: "O gods, let a boon desired from me be chosen by all of you; I shall grant it all. There is no need for hesitation in this matter. (35)
The gods said: "O Viṣṇu, since you are the granter of boons, grant us this boon: be born as the offspring of Aditi and become the younger brother of Śakra. (36)
Thus entreated by the gods, headed by Brahmā and Śakra, the Blessed One said, "So be it," and vanished right there.
Then, after some time, the Lord, the son of Aditi, who is infinite and assumes the form of Viṣṇu, became known as Vāmana because of his dwarf stature.
O Vyāsa, O best among the foremost of the twice-born, Bali, the son of Virocana, performed a hundred horse-sacrifices out of a desire to seize the kingdom of Indra.
Having appointed Kaśyapa as the officiating priest (ṛtvij) and the best of the Bhṛgus as the Hotṛ, the Grandfather himself became the Brahmā priest there. || 240 ||
The venerable Atri, the best of sages, became the Adhvaryu; Nārada was the Udgātṛ, and Vasiṣṭha was among the members of the assembly.
O Vyāsa, wherever all those lords of sages were appointed, there that best of kings, Bali, became initiated.
While the sacrifices were being conducted in this manner, O best of sages, let there be offerings made, food consumed, gifts bestowed, and likewise oblations poured.
O best of the twice-born, such auspicious words were heard there at that time; and amidst those wonderful sights, Vāmana, with a pure smile, arrived.
Chanting the mantras of the four Vedas from his mouth, O Indra among kings, that best of brahmins, Vāmana, stands at the gate.
O Vyāsa, everything was reported to the king by the doorkeeper; then the great king Bali, the son of Virocana, rose up.
Taking all that [offering], he went with his own courtiers and, having honored Vāmana, the creator of the worlds, according to the prescribed rule, [he returned].
Having brought him into the midst of the assembly and offered him a seat, he said: "O Brahmin, from where have you come? What is your desire? I shall surely grant it to you. (48)
Vāmana said: O Lord of kings, the entire creation belongs to Brahmā, the Supreme Lord; therefore, O Earth, I have come here with the desire to behold the sacrifice.
O sinless one, I have indeed seen the sacrifice of Varuṇa in the past; I have certainly also seen the sacrifice of the Lord of the Yakṣas.
O best of men, O great king, I have also witnessed the sacrifice of Dharma, of Prajāpati, and of Vāyu, all performed according to the prescribed rites.
O observer of great vows, even those sacrifices of the royal sages that have been seen by me are like the sacrifice which you, O great king, have witnessed.
O Indra among the lords of kings, there has never been such a one before, nor will there ever be; therefore, O sinless king, I have come here for the purpose of making a request of you. (53)
Bali said: "Ask, O best of the twice-born; what is your desire? I shall grant it to you. (54)
Vāmana said: "O Indra among the lords of kings, grant me three paces of land upon the earth for the sake of my dwelling, if it pleases you today, O best of monarchs. (55)

Bali said: "O Brahmin, what is this that you have requested? It is very little; it is not the best for you. Elephants, horses, chariots, the earth, and various kinds of jewels [are at your disposal]. (56)
"O best of the twice-born, request male and female servants, women of noble form, various riches, precious objects, and two bright garments. (57)
"You are a worthy recipient, you have accomplished all that is to be done, and you have mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences."
Vāmana said: "O King, O giver of honor, I have no desire for anything whatsoever on earth. Grant me three paces of land if you have faith in this now. (59)
When Vāmana had spoken thus, Bali then addressed these words: "O giver of honor, accept three paces of land for the sake of a dwelling."
Having spoken thus, O Vyāsa, that royal sage, impelled by destiny, gave the land to the twice-born even though he was restrained by Bhṛgu at that time.
As soon as the water was offered, Hari immediately stepped across the cosmic egg; together with him, the earth, including its mountains, forests, and groves, rose up two paces high.
Then, O Vyāsa, having conquered all the hosts of asuras and having bestowed the kingdom upon Śatakratu, Bali offered this wealth, the entire earth, as a tribute.
Afterwards, Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a dwarf, arrived at Kumudvatī.
Having established a sacred bathing place (tīrtha) originating from himself at the meritorious hermitage of Ṛddhisiddhi, O Vyāsa, that best of gods made his residence right there.

The sacred ford (tīrtha) established by Vāmana is called Vāmana-kuṇḍa; it occurs on the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī) in the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada, conjoined with the Śravaṇa asterism.
The Vāmana-dvādaśī is proclaimed to be the destroyer of ten million killings; when a man bathes in this sacred ford and fasts on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī), [he attains the supreme goal]. 67.
One should perform a vigil at night; it leads to becoming one with Brahman. Especially on the twelfth day (dvādaśī), they should perform great acts of charity.
For them, nothing whatsoever in the three worlds is difficult to obtain; thus indeed was the Vāmana Tīrtha described of old by the great seer.
It removes all sins, brings merit, and grants the boon of all desires; indeed, everything is obtained by him—there is no need for deliberation on this point. (270)
Sanatkumāra said: Hereafter I shall proclaim Vīreśvara; listen now. Having bathed in that sacred ford, a man shall attain the world of heroes (vīraloka). || 1 ||
The preeminent sacred ford of the Nāgas, which bestows the boon of all desires, is known by the name Kālabhairava; that sacred ford is remembered as supreme. || 2 ||
By the mere sight of whom one becomes transcendent over all suffering. || 3 ||
Vyāsa said: O best among the foremost of sages, at what time did this renowned holy site known as Kālabhairava become famous? Tell me this in detail.
Sanatkumāra said: In ancient times, this Bhairava was a yogi who caused terror among the yoginīs; at that time, the hosts of yoginīs were created as magical spells (kṛtyā) by Kālacakra.
Among them, the most excellent Yoginī is renowned as Kālī; by her, this stainless Bhairava has been constantly protected like a son.
By that, O best of beings, these faults and calamities—which are renowned on earth as being of three kinds and are supreme creators of all obstacles—are utterly shaken off.
Then, by that Supreme Soul, Kālakṛtyā was cast down; as were Mahāmārī, Pūtanā, Kṛtyā, Śakunī, Revatī, and Khalā.
Koṭarī and Tāmasī—these nine are remembered as Mātṛkās; they carry wicked defects, are evil, and cause fear to all living beings. || 9 ||
That righteous-souled one, who grants the boon of all desires, resides eternally at Vaśīcakra on the auspicious northern bank of the Śiprā.
Beyond the saline desert, he also remains forever; on a Sunday during the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha, one should remain composed there.
And on the ninth and eighth days, especially on the fourteenth day, those men who perform worship with steady minds— || 12 ||
On occasions such as marriage, the birth of a son, and other supreme auspicious ceremonies, one should worship with leaves, flowers, arka-gandha, and various kinds of food offerings (naivedya).

One should worship the Lord, who possesses the form of the Giver of Boons, with betel, perfumes, incense, and other offerings; one should constantly satisfy the omnipresent Lord with feasts for Brahmins and with fire oblations (homas). 14.
This is the supreme auspiciousness, this is the supreme blessing; having bowed to and praised that God for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals. (15)

May that Bhairava, who removes all impurities, who destroys the wicked and the rogue, who has long practiced his conduct, who moves about with a shaven head and a sacred grass girdle, who holds a skull in his hand, who wears earrings, who carries a staff, and who takes away worldly attachments, be the bestower of happiness. 16.

I shall constantly, evermore, remember the state of worldly existence—which is embellished by the play of various flavors, whose prowess is shaken by young brides, and in which even a cow’s footprint is made to reel by intoxication. 17.

O people, worship Bhairava, the Lord of Beings, who possesses eyes like the *amalaka* fruit and lotus, who is adorned with the beautiful moon, who is preeminent in all virtues, who assumes forms according to the desires of women, who has cast off all affliction, and who is the cause of the destruction of the *ḍākinīs*; he is the very embodiment of Śiva. (18)

O people, worship Bhairava, the Lord of Beings, who possesses the form of Śiva; he who destroys the strength of all forces, who is the sole protector of the field, whose neck is formidable and terrifying, who possesses a wide, boisterous laugh, who holds a sword in his hand, and who wears a serpent as a sacred thread.

O people, worship Bhairava, the Lord of Beings, who is the very form of Śiva; he who removes the fear of worldly existence, who causes terror to the Yoginīs, who is the sovereign of all the hosts of gods, whose eyes are as beautiful as the moon and sun, whose forehead is radiant with a crown, who wears a garland of pearls, and who is vast.

I worship Him who has four arms, who holds the conch and the mace as weapons, who is clad in yellow garments, whose splendor is like a dense rain-cloud, who bears the Śrīvatsa mark, whose neck is adorned by the Kaustubha gem, who bestows virtuous character, and who protects Śaṅkara. 21.

I take refuge in that Lord of Beings, who is delightful to the worlds, delightful to the universe, delightful to his beloved, delightful through his glory, delightful through his fame, and delightful through his ascetic power. 22.

I bow to Bhairava—the primordial, eternal Brahman, supremely pure, the bestower of perfection and desires, worthy of service by Hari, Hara, and the virtuous along with the creation itself; the fit object of yoga, contemplated by yogis, the sustainer of the ages, possessing a fitting countenance, the yogi who is complete, stainless, served by the good, and ever-present.
If a person recites this meritorious *Bhairavāṣṭaka* at the time of dawn, it shall destroy his bad dreams and bring about the fruit of his desired objects. (24)
At the king's gate, in a dispute, in battle, and likewise in a crisis; when commanded by an angry king, or when one has fallen into the hands of an enemy. || 25 ||
This should be recited with a concentrated mind for the destruction of the suffering of poverty; for them, nothing desired on earth shall remain difficult to attain. (26)

Thus ends the Bhairavāṣṭaka. At this sacred site (tīrtha), men who are terrified by the fear of saṃsāra should perform rites such as bathing and giving gifts; and when Bhairava is worshipped, he is most excellent. Therefore, with every effort, this supreme tīrtha should be utilized. || 27 ||

Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter, titled "Description of the Pilgrimage to Kālabhairava Tīrtha," in the Avantī-kṣetra-māhātmya of the fifth section (Āvantya-khaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Vyāsa said: O Brahmin, O best of beings, you who are illustrious have previously mentioned the Nāga-tīrtha; now tell me also of the greatness of that most excellent of holy places.
Furthermore, O best among the knowers of Brahman, I desire to hear from you: for how long was this proclaimed? Tell me in detail. (2)
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Brahmin, I shall relate before you the most meritorious story concerning the Nāga-tīrtha, which is supreme on earth as a destroyer of sins.
O scorcher of foes, merely by hearing it, a man becomes liberated from a curse; for in ancient times, the Nāgas fell from their state due to their mother’s curse.
Having been consumed by Janamejaya, they were indeed liberated by Āstika; then, O best of the twice-born, they questioned the son of Jaratkāru.
The Nāgas said: "O Brahman, by your grace we have been liberated from the consumer of oblations at this sacrifice of Janamejaya, in the presence of the King of the Gods."
O scorcher of enemies, seeking our welfare, please tell us of a place for our residence where, O Brahmin, a dwelling free from fear may always be established.
Āstīka said: "O best of maternal uncles, listen to that which is for your supreme welfare: there is indeed that place known as Kuśasthalī in the beautiful Mahākālavana. (8)
For on its southern side is the ancient, eternal Pūrvatīrtha, formerly called Nāgālaya, where Hari is ever present.
Having entered into yogic sleep, he rests in the eternal Brahman; renowned as "Śeṣaśāyī" (the one who reclines upon Śeṣa), he is praised throughout all the worlds.
The defect of the Kalpa does not afflict all embodied beings there; the sage Bakadālbhya, firm in his vows, performed penance in that place.
And the highly effulgent Lomaśa remains right there; the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya has attained a state of long life. 12.
The wheel of time does not turn there due to the majesty of Mahākāla; it is at that most excellent of sacred fords (tīrtha) where Kapila attained perfection.
Hariścandra was liberated from the censurable womb of a Caṇḍāla; those who were the foremost among the Seven Sages attained the state of Nirvāṇa.
For this reason, everyone should always rest there; the defect arising from your mother’s curse shall not afflict you at all. (15)
Having heard these words of the great ṛṣi Āstika, those best of serpents came there quickly for the purpose of dwelling.
Elāpatra, Kambala, Karkoṭaka, Dhanañjaya, Vāsuki the best of serpents, Takṣaka, and Nīla as well; (17)
Padmaka, Arbuda, and all those Nāgas indeed came here and, having observed their vows for a very long time, established their respective abodes.
There, O best of men, beautiful and supreme holy fords were produced; they created new ponds that became sacred sites.
They say that [these places] bestow great merit and remove great sins; there, the Siddhas, Gandharvas, and sages of rigid vows reside.
And it is always served by hosts of excellent groups of Apsarases, where in ancient times the great serpent Śeṣa was described by the great seer.
For the lotus-eyed Lord Viṣṇu, who reclines upon Śeṣa, is truly sufficient; all sacred fords on earth always abide there.
Renowned as Śvetadvīpa, its ground is adorned with jewels; there, indeed, are holy trees in full bloom on every side.
Swans, ducks, crows, and others, as well as cuckoos, kokilas, and cranes, and flocks of peacocks, dance there amidst the clusters of lotuses.
This great treasure-lake, Mahāpadma, is pure and scented by the wind carrying the fragrance of blue lotuses; it resounds with the songs of kinnaras.
Where well-adorned women and celestial nymphs sport, it is most wonderful, graced by beautiful daughters of the Nāgas.
Having bathed there, a person goes to the beautiful abode of Vaikuṇṭha, where Hari, the Lord of Ramā, reclines as Śeṣaśāyī.
Therein is a most beautiful holy site named Ramāsaras; having bathed there, a person always becomes possessed of prosperity—of this there is no doubt.
Thus, O Vyāsa, this supreme abode is the highest remover of all sins; right here is the supreme sacred site, the wonderful hermitage of Bali.
One should perform bathing and other rites here where Hari is present; at that very moment, a person becomes purified of all sins.
And for as many units of land as they give, for a period of time equal in number to their body hairs, [they shall enjoy the fruit]. (31)
Inexhaustible prosperity is attained by them, and their worlds are eternal, [if they perform this] on the new moon day in the month of Śrāvaṇa, or on the fifth lunar day, or on a Monday.
The worship of the Nāgas should be performed; the Śrāddha rite is ordained for the new moon (darśa). Thereby, the Śrāddha becomes inexhaustible and the desired object shall be attained. || 33 ||
Sanatkumāra said: Listen further, O Vyāsa, to the supreme and most excellent of all holy places—that sacred site of the high-souled Nṛsiṃha, which destroys all sins. 1.
Merely by the sight of whom one transcends all evil—he was formerly known as Hiraṇyakaśipu, the king of the Daityas.
Therefore, this entire earth has been seized by that evil-minded one; it is overrun by the forces of wicked Daityas, oppressed by their weight, and afflicted with grief.
Having become a cow with tearful face, she went to Brahmā for refuge along with the gods; seeing the Earth oppressed by the burden, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, [acted]. || 4 ||
He spoke in gentle words to dispel her fatigue: "Listen, O lady, to that which will be of benefit to you in this holy forest. (5)
I speak these words to you that are true and appropriate for this place and time: formerly, he performed a penance difficult for all embodied beings to perform.
By him, whose self was well-restrained, the meditation on the Gāyatrī was performed; and with a heart full of affection, a boon was granted to him by me.
Neither by day nor likewise by night, neither in the sky nor on the ground; neither with what is very dry nor with what is moist, nor by means of blows from missiles or weapons.
Neither by gods, asuras, nor gandharvas; nor by yakṣas, uragas, or kinnaras; nor by piśācas, guhyakas, and the like, nor ever by rākṣasas [can it be overcome]. || 9 ||
"May death not come to me from humans or from species of birds; [may it come] by the strike of a single palm of my hand, along with their kinsmen, armies, and vehicles. (10)
"That hero will kill me; he shall be my death. Having said "So be it," O King, I then became exceedingly joyful in heart toward him.
That Daitya of terrible command, possessing incomparable prowess, became the ruler of all worlds, both according to the sacred tradition and by his own worldly power. || 12 ||
Those very ones became authorized in the world and were freed from all distress; the lord of all the Daitya people constantly enjoyed the three worlds.
Therefore, you all should go to the Mahākāla forest of the Great Lord; there was a great sacred site there, the most excellent among all sacred sites.
To the south of Saṅgameśvara and likewise to the north of Karkarāja, on the auspicious bank of the Śiprā, there was formerly a place resembling Vaikuṇṭha.
The supreme abode named Nṛsiṃha has its sacred site established there; having gone there, O best of gods, perform rites such as bathing and giving gifts. (16)
"All of you, act with haste; you shall regain the worlds once more. Having heard his words, the gods, led by Indra, [acted accordingly]. || 17 ||
They reached Mahākālavana, where the milk-rich Śiprā flows; having dwelt on the bank of the Nṛsiṃha-tīrtha for eternal years.
Having performed bathing, giving of gifts, and likewise the worship of Nṛsiṃha, they have attained supreme perfection from this world by following such a procedure.
O Vyāsa, at that time, in the midst of the assembly, the preeminent among the Dānavas was slain by Hari, the slayer of enemies, in his own form as Nṛsiṃha.
Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain with a single blow of his trunk; thereafter, all the hosts of gods returned to their respective offices.
From that time forward, all the gods have always performed their midday worship at that very same sacred site where Lord Hari resides.
Thus, O Vyāsa, there exists on earth in Avanti a supreme holy ford (tīrtha). In this tīrtha, O best of the twice-born, rites such as bathing and giving gifts [yield great fruit]. (23)
Those men who perform meritorious deeds attain the supreme goal; this most excellent holy place (tīrtha) bestows merit at all times and on every occasion.
Once, having reached the fourteenth lunar day, the day sacred to Nṛsiṃha, he performed his ablutions and the worship of that wise Nṛsiṃha.
Whoever worships the Lord of Lords, Nṛsiṃheśvara, with a concentrated mind, prosperity will come into his hands; of this there is no doubt.
O Vyāsa, for him who beholds the god Agastyeśvara with a concentrated mind, nothing whatsoever on earth is seen to be difficult to attain.
There, Hanumān, the son of the Wind, attained supreme perfection—he who was a celibate student, of virtuous conduct, an ascetic, and the accomplisher of all goals. (28)
The supreme knower of destiny remains there for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals—at that banyan tree where, in ancient times, most difficult penance was performed.
By the ascetic son of Mitra and Varuṇa, for the sake of attaining perfection, two trees were designated: the Bodhi tree, known as Nyagrodha, and the Agasti-vaṭa.
A man, joined with his wife, should perform the Sāvitrī-vrata; O scorcher of foes, he shall obtain constant good fortune through Sāvitrī.
Having bathed at that sacred ford and having given a gift of good fortune—a vessel for the lineage complete with the eight auspicious marks along with its cloth—the man [attains his goal].
It is endowed with the seven types of grain, adorned with the five jewels, provided with fragrant garlands and the like, and joined with a crown and a sacred thread.
O scorcher of enemies, he who, according to his ability, fashions an image of Sāvitrī out of gold and gives it to a Brahmin learned in the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas— || 34 ||
One obtains vast, auspicious fortune that brings many enjoyments; having indeed experienced various pleasures, one shall again attain heaven. || 35 ||
A woman who performs the Sāvitrī-vrata becomes beloved by her husband; she is devoted to her husband, highly fortunate, and never becomes a widow. (36)
Listen, O Vyāsa, to the supreme and most excellent holy place renowned on earth; it is the Great Lord (Maheśvara) who is celebrated by the name Kuṭumbeśvara. || 1 ||
That excellent holy place is a sacred ford that bestows the fruits of all holy places; having bathed in that ford, a man certainly becomes a householder.
In ancient times, Dakṣa, the lord of progeny, performed austerities for the sake of his family; formerly, O Vyāsa, his sixty sons were exiled by Nārada.
Desirous of offspring, that righteous-souled one of great splendor practiced a vow for a very long time together with his wife, abstaining from food and having conquered his senses.
O Vyāsa, having bathed pure at this sacred ford and chanting the eternal Brahman, he performed most rigorous penance for ten thousand years.
By the grace of that sacred ford (tīrtha), he shall obtain abundant progeny; thus known as Prajāpati, the powerful Dakṣa was born.
Even Brahmā, having performed extremely difficult penance there afterwards, attained at that very moment the form of the partless lotus.
Mahādeva also arrived at that very place, the abode of Brahmā; O best of beings, even today the four-faced Liṅga is seen there.
The goddess known as Bhadrakālī, who bears the auspicious seat, always sports right there, O Vyāsa, having taken up her vows.
Right there at the gate stands Bhairava, the protector of the field (kṣetrapālaka), who in former times had become lame in one foot due to being afflicted by a preeminent Daitya.
Constantly protected by the Goddess like a son, he always remains in that place; all those hosts of gods are established in that sacred ford (tīrtha).
Even the highly fortunate sages always come to this river, which bestows many sons, at every festival juncture for the purpose of performing their twilight prayers.
Those men who perform their ablutions at this sacred ford with virtuous conduct will find nothing difficult to attain throughout birth after birth. (13)
During terrible great afflictions and during great pestilences, those intent upon them perform oblations constantly with mustard seeds, black mustard, and barley.
Through various offerings of milk-rice and enjoyments, no fault arises for them, even in times of famine, loss of kingdom, or in an exceedingly terrible battle.
One should worship the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla) with a concentrated mind during every calamity; one becomes liberated from all suffering—of this there is no doubt. || 16 ||
Having bathed at the Kuṭumbaka Tīrtha and having worshipped Maheśvara, one should give a pumpkin as a gift to an ascetic Brāhmaṇa.
Endowed with gold, jewels, pearls, clothing, and ornaments, and possessed of wealth and grain, such a man is born as a householder.
O Vyāsa, that which is the fourteenth day in the bright fortnight of Phālguna, joined with the thirteenth, is likewise called Śivarātri.
On that day, a man, having bathed, should perform a vigil at night, [worshipping] with bilva water, fragrances, and many flowers and fruits.
The man who worships with devotion the supreme Lord of the Mountain, together with his attendants, using incense, lamps, food offerings, garments, ornaments, and other such things; ||| 21 ||
His sin goes to destruction, and he is glorified in the world of Śiva; that man on earth obtains the merit of twelve Ekādaśīs.
For him, the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice accrues at every moment during that vigil; then, having risen in the morning, he should perform the rites of bathing, giving gifts, and so forth.
O Vyāsa, having performed the worship and adoration of Śiva according to the prescribed rules, one should feed seven Brahmins; hear now the meritorious fruit thereof. || 24 ||
One obtains the fruit of fourteen thousand Vājapeya sacrifices by [giving] fourteen thousand tawny cows with their calves; it is not otherwise.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, to the account of the most meritorious and supremely beautiful holy site known as Devaprayāga, which destroys all sins. || 1 ||
And there is the supreme abode of the gods, where the sacred ford (tīrtha) is located, O scorcher of foes; it is situated on the northern part of Somatīrtha and to the south of Prayāga.
And on the eastern side of Kṣiprā, a sacred bathing place (tīrtha) is established; having bathed at that tīrtha, a man should behold the Supreme God.
To him who [worships] the god known as Mādhava, who bestows all fruits upon the earth, the Lord of Gods, the Master of the Universe, grants his desired object. || 4 ||
There resides Ānandabhairava, who is saluted by all the gods; by the mere sight of him, the destruction of all sins occurs.
O Vyāsa, never does terrible torment arise for him; O Vyāsa, that man always remains fearless at the gateway to heaven.

In the month of Jyeṣṭha, during the bright fortnight, on the tenth lunar day, when Mercury is in conjunction with the asterism Hasta, under the Vyatīpāta yoga, when the Moon is in Virgo and the Sun is in Taurus—on this occasion, O child, the Daśālā festival arises, which is the supreme, pure birth of the Gaṅgā.
On that day, a man who bathes shall obtain the fruit of all holy fords (tīrthas). Now listen, O Vyāsa, to the supreme and unbroken holy ford beyond this.
O Brahmin, in ancient times there was a certain Brāhmaṇa, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, for whom no violation of his vow occurred merely by hearing this.
Renowned as Dharmaśarman, he was devoted to virtuous conduct, pure, observant of many vows, self-controlled, and a master of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences.
Due to the occurrence of some fault, the completion of his vow did not take place; thus, after a great deal of time had passed, Nārada, who beholds the gods, [arrived].
O Brahmin, when that great ascetic came to his house for the sake of hospitality, the twice-born man would always rise up with great respect.
O Bhūman, having honored Nārada with rites prescribed by rule and having worshipped him, that best of the twice-born questioned the most excellent of sages.
O Blessed One, everything is known by you through the eye of wisdom; yet, O Sinless One, a certain great fault previously arose among us.
"O Lord, tell me the reason why a transgression of my vow has certainly occurred through this association with sin; for what fault can be reckoned here? (15)
Nārada said: Listen, O best of the twice-born, to what was performed by you in the past. In Mahārāṣṭra there was a very famous Brāhmaṇa named Dhanasañcaka. || 16 ||
This Brahmin named Brahmadatta was a reviler of the Vedas and the Brāhmaṇas; he was greedy for wealth, overbearing, and turned away from all righteous duties.
An atheist regarding gods and sacred fords, a stealer of others' property, one constantly devoted to the wives of others, a gambler, and a thief— (18)
Thus, with his life-span exhausted, he then became destitute of wealth; fallen and deeply distressed, he wandered here and there on the bank of a river. (19)
Having gone forth in the pursuit of theft, he associated with travelers; after some time, that man of wicked character, afflicted by disease, met his death. (20)
At that moment, the brahmin, who had committed many sins, was led by the servants of Yama to Saṃyaminī; having reached the city of King Yama, the twice-born man arrived there.
Then that man, who was devoted to his wife, was seen by Dharmarāja; having observed him, he suddenly spoke these words consistent with righteousness: ||| 22 ||
Listen, all you servants, with one-pointed minds: everything that has been performed by this man is evil action and every kind of sin. (23)
A sinner who dies on the bank of the Godāvarī does not incur any fault from us; for there are thirty-five million sacred fords (tīrthas) present there day and night.
They came to the banks of the Gautamī even when Jupiter was situated in Leo; at the end of their lives, the touch of the wind occurred upon their physical bodies.
"By the power of that merit, there shall be no cause for harm to us anywhere; therefore, O attendants, you must not seize him, but let him go! (26)
Thus liberated by them, the Brahmin returned once more to the state of Brahmā; yet, due to that attachment to sin, he fell to earth as one whose vows were broken.
The Brāhmaṇa said: O Brahman, by what means may the destruction of all sins occur? What is the penance, what is the gift, and what is the service of sacred fords and vows? (28)
By the power of which merit, no violation of the vow occurs. || 29 ||
Nārada said: Listen, O best among the foremost of the twice-born, to that which is known as Mahākālavana, where the lake of Rudra was described by the seer who perceives the truth.
O best of the twice-born, millions upon millions of excellent holy fords exist; therefore, O twice-born one, this eternal place is renowned as Koṭitīrtha.
To the north of that holy site is a supreme tirtha that grants all desires, renowned by the name Akhaṇḍasara, located in the vicinity of Akhaṇḍeśvara.
By the mere sight of whom one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices; therefore, my child, go there by all means without delay.
Having heard these words of his, O Vyāsa, that twice-born man went to Kumudvatī; having bathed in Akhaṇḍasaras and beheld the god Maheśvara.
"O best of the twice-born, that most excellent great tirtha, Akhandeshvara, has indeed been reached immediately by those who possess merit; thus it is, O Vyasa. (35)

Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of Akhaṇḍeśvara," in the *Avantī-kṣetra-māhātmya* of the fifth section (*Āvantya-khaṇḍa*) within the *Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa*, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen further to the supreme sacred site that bestows the fruit of all sacred sites; it was formerly proclaimed by Brahmā when Mārkaṇḍeya questioned him.
Listen, my child: on the surface of the earth, there is the most divine river Śiprā; on its bank is an excellent holy site (tīrtha) renowned as Karkarāja. || 2 ||
By the mere sight of whom there occurs the destruction of great sins; he is the Moon, born from Lake Mānasa, who pacifies all mental afflictions. || 3 ||
When the sun has moved to its position there, performing the southern solstice, it is declared to be the three seasons known as Vidhūmrārcis. || 4 ||
O scorcher of foes, even those yogins who have died during the Cāturmāsya while Hari is asleep, if they are men devoid of vows, continue [to suffer] there.
O child, I tell you the truth: there is no good rebirth for those who die during the four months of the rainy season, nor for those who die during the southern course of the sun.
For the sake of their upliftment, this sacred ford was created; it is celebrated throughout all the worlds as Karkarāja.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: "O Blessed One, O Lord of the World, this entire universe, both moving and unmoving, has been created by you, who possess the form of the cosmos."
O best among the knowers of Brahman, I wish to hear from you the rules for righteous conduct during the four-month period when Hari is asleep. (9)
Brahmā said: Listen, my child, to the supreme merit and auspicious fruit of the Cāturmāsya, hearing which liberation is not difficult for men to attain within the land of Bhārata. (10)
This Blessed One is the bestower of liberation and the cause for crossing over saṃsāra; by the mere remembrance of him, the destruction of all sins occurs. (11)
Human birth is difficult to obtain in this world, and within that, noble lineage; within that, self-restraint, and therein, auspicious association with the virtuous. (12)
Where there is no association with the virtuous, no devotion to Viṣṇu, and no observance of vows—especially during Cāturmāsya—one who performs the vow of Viṣṇu is truly auspicious.
For one who remains without vows during the Cāturmāsya period, his merit is rendered fruitless; so too are all holy fords, gifts, and sacred shrines.
When the Cāturmāsya period arrives, they remain taking refuge in Viṣṇu; that Viṣṇu always takes refuge in the excellent holy place known as Karkarāja.
And his life is truly auspicious with a well-nourished body, by whom Hari was worshipped when the Cāturmāsya period arrived. (16)
The gods, having granted him boons for as long as he lives, have achieved their purpose; yet, having obtained a human body, he remains averse to the Cāturmāsya vow.
They say that hundreds of sins reside within his body, without a doubt; for human birth is difficult to attain in this world, and devotion to Hari is even more difficult to find. (18)

Especially during the Cāturmāsya, while the Lord Janārdana is asleep, a man who bathes at Karkarātra during the Cāturmāsya, O best of the twice-born, and first effects the purification of his body, shall attain the path of liberation. (19)
Even there, whether at a waterfall, a well, a pond, or a lake, the merit is declared by the gods and demons to be even greater than that.
Whoever bathes in them constantly, for him there shall be the destruction of sin.
Therefore, this river has been declared more meritorious than others by the gods and asuras, whether at Puṣkara, Prayāga, or wherever there is a great body of water. (23)
But for one who bathes during the Cāturmāsya period at the confluence of the Revā with the ocean in the eastern Bhāskara-kṣetra, the merit is even greater than that.
He who bathes for even a single day during the Cāturmāsya period does not experience suffering; and he who, with a concentrated mind, bathes for three days in the Narmadā river [attains the same].
When the Lord of the Universe is asleep, sin is divided a thousandfold; yet he who bathes in the Godāvarī at the break of dawn for even a single fortnight [attains this merit].

Having shattered the body born of karma, he goes to the same world as Viṣṇu. In Avantī, at Karkarāja, a man becomes Viṣṇu in person; even if he should transgress [the rules] during Cāturmāsya for a single moment or half a moment, [he attains this].

I do not know the extent of the superior fruit for one who bathes with water mixed with sesame and *amala* seeds, or even with *bilva* water; what has been ordained by the sages for such a person, and of what nature is it? || 28 ||
He who constantly remembers the Gaṅgā while near a well has produced that water of the Gaṅgā; with it, he should perform his bath. || 29 ||
Even the Gaṅgā, flowing from the big toe of the God of gods, is declared to be a destroyer of sins at all times, and especially during the Cāturmāsya.
During the Cāturmāsya period, Lord Nārāyaṇa resides within the water; bathing there is superior to all holy places, as it is infused with a portion of Viṣṇu’s own splendor.
A tenfold bath should be performed with the name of Viṣṇu, which yields great fruit; especially when the Lord is asleep, a man may attain divinity.
O Brahmin, whatever auspicious and meritorious rite is performed without bathing becomes fruitless; indeed, the Rākṣasas seize it.
Through bathing one attains truth; in truth resides the eternal Dharma. Having reached the path of liberation through Dharma, one never again falls into despair. || 34 ||
Those who know the inner self, those who are meritorious, and those who have reached the further shore of the Vedanta—they are purified by bathing in the gift of all things.
For Hari indeed dwells, having taken recourse to the body of one who has performed his ablutions; in such [bodies], the fruit of all actions becomes fully realized.
For the destruction of all sins and for the propitiation of the deities, bathing in water during the Cāturmāsya period brings about the eradication of all evil.
One should not bathe at night, nor during the twilight hours except during an eclipse; one should not bathe with hot water at night, for purity is not thereby attained.
Purification through the sight of the sun is prescribed for all ritual acts; however, during the Cāturmāsya period, purification by water is especially ordained.
But when the body is incapable [of bathing], one becomes pure by means of a bath with ashes, O best of Brahmins, or by a bath with mantras, or with the water from the feet of Viṣṇu.
One should perform ablutions before Nārāyaṇa at sacred sites, holy fords, and in rivers—especially in the Śiprā river and at the excellent holy ford named Karka.
The man who bathes there constantly attains the station of Viṣṇu; therefore, O best of the Bhārgavas, go there without delay.
Whatever holy fords and sacred shrines exist upon the earth, they all reside eternally within the waters of Karkarāja.
And those men who perform their ablutions when the lord of the day (the Sun) is situated in Cancer—for them there is no return [to this world] even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Having arrived for the four-month period, I dwell right there; on the surface of the universe, there is no river as meritorious as the Revā. (45)
There is no god other than Maheśa who bestows liberation, nor any other than Janārdana; there is no city equal to Ujjayinī that grants the boons of desire.
O child, there is no sacred ford on the surface of the earth equal to Karkarāja; by the mere sight of it, a man becomes a partaker of liberation.
Thus, O Vyāsa, it was narrated by Brahmā to Bhārgava; therefore, with every effort, go to Mahākālavana.
And for us as well, there is a most beautiful place right there during the four months while Hari is asleep, until the awakening night arrives.
For that duration, there is liberation right there, without a doubt; provided one casts off the body while Hari is asleep during the Cāturmāsya period.
A long residence in the world of Yama arises; of this there is no doubt. Therefore, [one should reside] in a portion of Tulasī, at Śāligrāma, or in a temple of the gods. || 51 ||
Having staked one's very self, O best of the twice-born, one should apply oneself to that very task until the awakening Dvādaśī arrives.
Afterwards, having liberated [the image] with ghee and gold, one should lead it back to its own place; then the fault arising from the four-month period shall not afflict that person.
O Vyāsa, for one who performs a bath in the waters of the Śiprā at Karkarāja, such an excellent holy site arises, bestowing the fruit of all sacred fords.
O best of the twice-born, whatever sacred fords, rivers, and oceans exist upon the earth, they all assemble during the Cāturmāsya.
And for that reason, that excellent holy site is remembered as Karkarāja. || 56 ||
Those who indeed hear this meritorious narrative or cause it to be heard, for them never arises any fault arising from the Cāturmāsya period. (57)
Sanatkumāra said: On the southern side of Meru and likewise to the north of Dugdhakuṇḍa, there is Ṛṣabha, the best of mountains, frequented by gods and Gandharvas.
O twice-born one, where the beautiful celestial damsels sport constantly, there stands a lake named Ramyasara, which grants all desires.
Having bathed at that sacred ford, a man certainly becomes fortunate; he sports eternally with the gods and becomes supremely renowned upon the earth.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada, conjoined with the Maitra constellation (Anurādhā), one should arrive here on that day and perform rites such as bathing and giving gifts.
O Vyāsa, eternal worlds are constantly prepared for them; there is a divine and most beautiful sacred site (tīrtha) on the northeastern side of Mount Meru.
It is renowned as Bindusara, the bestower of all desired boons; there flow the Gaṅgā, the meritorious Sarasvatī, and the Payasvinī Śarayū.
O son of Satyavatī, these best of rivers have gone there, as well as those who are Siddhas and Sādhyas, and ascetics firm in their vows.
People always performed worship there at that sacred ford; having bathed in that ford, a man certainly attains all his goals.
The fourth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Bhādrapada is indeed proclaimed as always being Siddhā, for it was on that day that the Lord of the Gaṇas was born.

He is renowned as Manah-kameshvara, the bestower of all desired boons. Having bathed in his sacred pool and beheld the god Ganeshvara, a man shall attain a hundred heart's desires and become a master who moves at will.
Vyāsa said: O Brahmin, in this auspicious field, the most excellent Mahākālavana, || 11 ||
How many in number are the sacred fords (tīrthas) and the abodes of the gods? Tell us in detail about whatever ones are renowned.
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, best of sages, to this supreme narrative that removes all sins, concerning the sacred fords and the *liṅgas* that exist in Avantī, O great sage. (13)
Even the self-born, four-faced Brahmā himself would be unable to describe them fully for sixty thousand years, nor could he ever speak of them in any other way.
As many drops as fall from the garlands of clouds, as many blades of grass upon the earth, and likewise as many grains of sand on the earth; || 15 ||
No one is able to state the number of luminaries in the sky; likewise, O ascetic, there is no end to the number of holy fords and lingas in Avantī. (16)
This city is a sacred pilgrimage site both in the intermediate space and upon the earth; it possesses ponds, wells, tanks, and the like, as well as springs and flowing streams.
Rivers, lakes, and excavated pools are indeed sacred fords in every respect; nevertheless, listen to me as I speak of them in connection with the procession of the gods.
Whatever matters are most essential, those I shall declare to you; by knowing which, you will be eternally liberated from the effects of previously performed good and evil deeds. (19)
He who, having risen early in the morning, is always pure and disciplined in mind, and is endowed with the remembrance of Viṣṇu, [performs] all activities such as the fulfillment of desires.
Having prepared all types of perfumes along with sesame seeds and unbroken grains (akṣata), and having bathed in the Rudrasaras, O dear one, one should likewise observe the vow.
A procession for the deity is especially recommended during the months of Ūrja and Mādhava, as well as Vaiśākha and Āṣāḍha, and particularly on the occasion of Śivarātri.

In whichever sacred bathing place (tīrtha) belongs to a particular deity, and in the presence of whichever deity it may be, one should indeed perform an ablution there as well as the worship of that deity.
He who performs [the rite] according to the prescribed rule enjoys the full fruit; therefore, with every effort, one should undertake the procession of the deity. (24)
Vyāsa said: "O Brahmin, in what manner should a man perform the pilgrimage to the gods? O ascetic, I wish to hear all of that in detail. (25)

Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, I shall proclaim the supreme secret as I have heard it—the dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara concerning the rites of the divine procession and other ceremonies. (26)

Umā said: "O Lord Maheśvara, let the power of this sacred field be told; O Best of Speakers, O Supporter of the Earth, tell me from the very beginning which holy fords (tīrthas) exist there and which Liṅgas are present. (27)
Īśvara said: Listen with diligence, O Goddess, to the power that destroys sins.
O Great Goddess, this primordial field is always exceedingly dear to me, where the divine and most meritorious Śiprā, my beloved new river, flows.
The confluence of the Nīlagangā and likewise the Gandhavatī river—these four rivers are dear to me at Kumudvatī, O lady of virtuous vows.
There are eighty-four Īśvaras as well as eight Bhairavas; likewise, the Rudras are eleven, and the Ādityas are recorded as twelve.
"O auspicious lady, there are indeed six Vināyakas and twenty-four goddesses here in this most excellent Mahākālavana, from which I have come."
O auspicious one, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and all others are indeed established right here; O Goddess, this sacred field, extending for a yojana, is pervaded by the gods.
Viṣṇu is proclaimed to have ten [forms]; hear their names from me: Vāsudeva, Ananta, Balarāma, and Janārdana. (34)
Nārāyaṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, the Boar who supports the earth, Viṣṇu in the form of Vāmana, He who reclines upon Śeṣa, and the abode of Śrī. || 35 ||
These ten are declared to be the supreme Vaiṣṇavas, who remove all sins.
Umā said: "O Blessed One, I desire to hear in due order about those lords of the gods who dwell in the delightful Mahākālavana."
Tell me the names of those Vināyakas, Bhairavas, and goddesses who are the sons of the Wind; likewise, tell me the names of the Rudras, Ādityas, and others.

Īśvara said: The Lord of the Gaṇas is eternally the bestower of prosperity, the bestower of supernatural powers, and the granter of desires; he is the destroyer of obstacles, full of joy, and fond of the vow of the fourth lunar day (Caturthī-vrata). || 39 ||
These six are indeed declared to be supreme destroyers of obstacles; Umā, Caṇḍīśvarī, and Gaurī bestow prosperity and spiritual accomplishments upon men. (40)
Vaṭayakṣiṇī and Vīrabhadra—these are the eight Mothers (Mātṛs). Also Mahāmāyā, the renowned Satī, Kapālamātṛkā, Ambikā, Śītalā, and Ekānaṃśā, who bestows success (Siddhi). || 42 ||
Brahmāṇī and Pārvatī, the Yoginī endowed with yoga, Kaumārī and the Goddess Bhagavatī, as well as the six Kṛttikās. || 43 ||
The Carpaṭāmātṛkās are renowned, as are the Vaṭamātṛs; Sarasvatī is likewise well-known, and Mahālakṣmī is indeed remembered.
The sixty-four Yoginīs are known as the Mātṛkās; they are remembered as Kālikā, Mahākālī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Brahmacāriṇī. (45)
Vaiṣṇavī is likewise proclaimed, as well as Vārāhī, Viṃdhyavāsinī, Ambā, and Ambālikā; these are the twenty-four supreme [forms]. (46)
Hanumān, Brahmācārī, and the mighty Kumāra—these four sons of the Wind-god have indeed been described by me to you. (47)
Daṇḍapāṇi, Vikrānta, Mahābhairava, Sitāsita, Baṭuka, Bālaka, Nandin, and another, Pañcāśatika—these are the six. || 48 ||

And Kālabhairava is renowned as the eighth guardian of the field (kṣetrapāla). These eight Bhairavas are celebrated as supreme removers of great sins: Kapardī, Kapālī, Kalānātha, and Vṛṣāsana. || 49 ||

He is the three-eyed one, the wielder of the trident, clad in bark garments or naked as the directions; he is the lord of the mountains, the mover at will, the all-pervading one whose every limb is adorned.
And the eleven Rudras are proclaimed as the destroyers of the enemy faction: Aruṇa, Sūrya, Vedāṅga, Bhānu, Indra, Ravi, and Aṃśumān. || 51 ||
Suvarṇaretas, Ahaḥkartṛ, Mitra, Viṣṇu, and Sanātana—these are the twelve Ādityas, the supreme removers of all diseases. || 52 ||
O Daughter of Himācala, listen as I constantly recite the names of the forty-four Liṅgas, the foremost of which is Agastyeśvara.
Agastyeśvara is proclaimed first, and after that Guheśvara; then Ḍhuṇḍheśvara is mentioned, and then Ḍamarukeśvara, O beautiful lady. (54)
Śambhu is the Lord of the beginningless aeon; the supreme Svarṇajāleśvara; the god Triviṣṭapeśvara; and the one known as Kapāleśvara. || 55 ||
Śambhu as Karkoṭakeśvara, and after that Siddheśvara; then Rudra as Svargadvāreśvara, and another as Lokapāleśvara. || 56 ||
He is renowned as Kāmeśvara; after that, Kuṭumbeśvara; he is renowned as Indradyumneśvara; and after that, Īśāneśa. || 57 ||
The deity known as Apsareśvara, as well as Kalkaleśvara, and another god named Nāmacaṇḍeśvara, who removes sins during the day. || 58 ||
Pratihāreśvara and Kukkuṭeśa after that; then the meritorious Meghanādeśvara and the supreme Mahākāleśvara. || 59 ||
Mukteśvara is fully described; after that is Someśvara; the deity Anarakeśvara, and after that, Jaṭeśvara. || 60 ||
Rāmeśvara is Mahādeva, and after that is Cyavaneśa; Akhaṇḍeśa is well-known, and Pattaneśa is remembered after that. || 61 ||
Then Ānandeśa is proclaimed, and after that Kaṇṭhaḍeśa; then the one renowned as Indreśvara, and after that Mārkaṇḍeśa. (62)
Śiveśvara is proclaimed [as the first], and after that Kusumeśa; then the one renowned as Akrūra, and after that Kuṇḍeśvara. || 63 ||
Lumpeśvara is fully proclaimed, and after that Gaṅgeśvara; the one renowned as Śūleśvara is remembered next, and then Oṃkāreśa.
Kaṇṭakeśa, Mahārudra, and thereafter Siṃheśvara; Revanteśvara is the supreme deity, preceded by Ghaṇṭeśvara. || 65 ||
Mahādeva Prayāgeśvara, and after that Siddheśvara; the supreme deity Mātaṅgeśvara, and then the excellent Saubhāgyeśa. || 66 ||
Rūpeśvara is renowned, and after that, Brahmeśvara; then the god Jalpeśvara, and likewise Kedāreśvara. (67)
Piśāceśvara-Śambhu, and beyond that Saṅgameśa; then the famous Durdharṣeśa, and after that Caṇḍādityeśvara. || 68 ||
Karabheśvara is declared to be supreme; Śiva Rājasthaleśvara is proclaimed next; thereafter Vaḍaleśvara is mentioned, and Aruṇeśa is remembered after that. || 69 ||
The deity Puṣpadanteśvara, then Avimukteśvara; the deity Hanumateśvara, and thereafter Viśveśvara. (70)
The one known as Svapneśvara, and after him Siddheśvara; then the god Nīlakaṇṭheśvara, and after that Sthāvareśa. (71)
Kāmeśvara is proclaimed [first], and after that Pratihāreśvara; Paśupatīśvara is proclaimed, and Viśveśvara is beyond that; Svarṇajāleśvara is proclaimed, and after that Manaḥkāmeśvara. || 72 ||
That [liṅga] is named Durvāseśvara; after that is Nāgacaṇḍeśvara; then the famous Kharpareśa, and after that Brahmeśvara.
The one known as Pātāleśvara is proclaimed, and after that, Gupteśvara; the one named Kapileśvara, and beyond him, Yogayogeśvara. (74)
The supreme one known as Bhīmeśvara is called Dhanuḥsahasra; Agnīśvara is declared to be supreme, and Deveśvara is beyond even that.
The Lord of Daśāśvamedhika is celebrated as Dvādaśārka; Gadādhareśvara is renowned, and Śambhurāja is known as Vaijanātha.
Somanātheśvara is renowned, and after him follows Ghuṣmeśvara; the one named Bhīmaśaṅkara comes next, and after that is Ghaṇṭeśvara. || 77 ||
The one known as Ūṣareśvara, the supreme Candrādityeśvara, the one celebrated as Keśavārka, and the supreme Śaktibhedeśvara; || 78 ||
Rāmeśvara is the supreme deity; Vālmīkeśvara is Śaṅkara; Jvāleśvara is declared to be Śiva; and beyond that is Abhayeśa. (79)
Vighnahasteśvara is proclaimed, and after that Cañcaleśa; the one renowned as Puruṣottama, and after that Vīreśvara. || 80 ||
And Karṇeśvara is renowned, and after that Pṛthukeśa; Ānandeśa is renowned, and after that Koṭeśvara. || 81 ||
Avimukteśvara is proclaimed, and Hanumatkeśvara is supreme; he is renowned as Vimaleśvara, and Candreśvara is beyond that. || 82 ||
Bindukeśa is renowned, as well as the one known as Vālukeśvara; then there is the god Bṛhaspatīśvara, and after that, Asaṃkhyāteśvara.
O best of beings, whatever sacred fords (tīrthas) there may be, they exist there as Liṅgas; they are to be worshipped and honored in every way.
All four gatekeepers have been recognized by those great-souled ones; O best of the twice-born, he who is renowned as Piṅgaleśvara is at the eastern gate.
Likewise, at the southern gate is Kāyāvarohaṇeśvara; he who is renowned as Bilvakeśvara is stationed at the western gate. (86)
Then Dardureśvara is proclaimed at the gate known as the North; these and many others are the lords of the three worlds, designated as Liṅgas. || 87 ||
Indeed, sixty-six trillion purifying [tīrthas] are proclaimed to be in the delightful Mahākālavana. (88)
O Vyāsa, the number of Liṅgas in Mahākālavana is not known; nevertheless, they have been described by me here according to their primary importance. (89)
Whatever sacred ford (tīrtha) belongs to whichever deity, it is proclaimed by that deity’s name; having bathed and given a gift there, one obtains the fruit of that specific tīrtha.
Likewise, O sinless one, the nine auspicious planets were proclaimed of old; hear now their meritorious names and their corresponding sacred fords (tīrthas). || 91 ||
He is renowned as Narāditya; after him is Someśvara; he is celebrated as Maṅgaleśvara; and after that is Budheśvara.
Bṛhaspatīśvara has been proclaimed, as well as Śiva as Śukreśvara; Mahādeva is likewise designated as Sthāvareśvara by the lords of sages.
O best of beings, Rāhu and Ketu are well-known; their sacred fords exist there, and by bathing in those fords, a man is liberated from all sins.
The planets bestow sovereignty, and the planets take away sovereignty; indeed, the entire three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile, are pervaded by the planets. 95.
Having bathed at Grahatīrtha, a man should perform the worship of the planets; indeed, the affliction of the planets shall never trouble him. (96)
Thus, O Vyāsa, the gods and the sacred fords have been fully described by me; this pilgrimage is most meritorious, supreme, purifying, and destructive of sin.
For the sake of uplifting those who suffer from fierce planetary afflictions, terrible poverty, and dire distress, the Devayātrā is proclaimed. 98.
For those best of men who constantly perform the inner domestic rites within the sacred field, nothing whatsoever remains difficult to attain in the three worlds.
A sonless man obtains a son, a poor man shall acquire wealth; a Brahmin becomes learned in the sciences, and a Kṣatriya becomes victorious. 100.
His lineage becomes inexhaustible, and he is glorified in the world of Śiva. || 101 ||
Vyāsa said: O Blessed One, you who possess a divine form have related everything—the sacred majesty of the Avanti-tīrtha, which is equal to the Vedas.

Furthermore, O best among the knowers of Brahman, O most excellent of beings, O observer of noble vows, I wish to hear from you how many sacred fords (tīrthas) exist here in the delightful Mahākālavana at Avanti on this earth. || 2 ||
Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O best of the twice-born, to this supreme narrative that removes all sins.
O best of the twice-born, this dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara was formerly asked by the wise Nārada; this very question was posed by Nārada in the past.
Nārada said: O Blessed One, I desire to hear; tell us in detail about those holy fords (tīrthas) that exist in the auspicious Mahākāla forest.
O sinless Brahmin, having been thus questioned by Nārada in the past, Hara, accompanied by Umā, spoke with gentle words.
The illustrious Mahādeva said: Listen, O best of sages, O observer of noble vows; I shall describe those holy fords (tīrthas) that exist within the auspicious Mahākālavana.
Whatever sacred fords (tīrthas) exist on the surface of the earth, beginning with Puṣkara, they all reside within the supreme Mahākālavana.
O seventh one, innumerable thousands and millions upon millions of beings immerse themselves in the Rudrasaras; thus it is called Koṭitīrtha.
In winter, at the Paishacamocana tirtha on the mountain, the Kinnaras shower a rain of frost-droplets; this is indeed seen there.
O best of beings, I do not indeed know the number of holy places on earth; how many sacred fords (tīrthas) and likewise lingas exist? (11)
Nevertheless, O best of beings, O most excellent of the twice-born, I shall describe according to their importance all the days of the year.
O scorcher of enemies, so many [pilgrims] are known to arrive; and when a full year has passed, one becomes an Avanti-yātrika.
He who performs this according to the prescribed rule shall become Śambhu himself; and whatever fruit is obtained from residing in Kāśī for thousands of Manvantaras, [that he shall obtain].
That fruit is produced at Avantī in five days during the month of Vaiśākha; therefore, a pilgrimage to Avantī must be performed with great effort by one who desires liberation.
One should especially perform the ritual bath at Avantī during the month of Mādhava; for indeed, O Vyāsa, that man who reaches Avantī during the month of Vaiśākha—
Having observed the vow for a year and bathed at every sacred ford according to the prescribed rule, one who has given all manner of gifts enjoys the fruit together with its very root.
Having enjoyed vast pleasures, he is glorified in the world of Śiva.
This majesty increases devotion to Śiva, brings fame, and augments merit; whoever causes it to be heard or listens to it with devotion shall uplift their lineage and go to the abode of Hara. (19)

Now begins the second [chapter], the *Māhātmya* of the eighty-four *liṅgas* situated in Avantī, within the fifth *Avantya-khaṇḍa* of the glorious *Skanda Mahāpurāṇa*. Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa! Salutations to Śrī Mahākāla! Now begins the *Māhātmya* of the eighty-four *liṅgas* situated in Avantī, within the *Avantya-khaṇḍa*. Umā said: "Please describe with effort those holy places (*tīrthas*) on earth as well as the meritorious rivers, in which the ancestral rite (*śrāddha*) is offered. (1)
Īśvara said: There is in the worlds the renowned Gaṅgā, who flows through the three paths; she is served by gods and Gandharvas and frequented by sages.
The goddess Yamunā, daughter of Tapa, is the purifier of the world; she is the beloved of the ancestors, O Goddess, and the remover of great sins. (3)
The Candrabhāgā, the Vitastā, and the Narmadā at Amarakaṇṭaka; Kurukṣetra, O Goddess, Gayā, Prabhāsa, and likewise Naimiṣa.
Kedāra, Puṣkara, and likewise Kāyāvarohaṇa, as well as the most meritorious and auspicious Mahākālavana, O Goddess. (5)
Where the illustrious Mahākāla resides, the fire that consumes the fuel of sins, the sacred field extending for a yojana destroys even the sin of killing a Brahmin.

This sacred field bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, destroying the impurities of the Kali age; it is imperishable even at the time of universal dissolution, O Goddess, and difficult to attain even for the gods.
Umā said: "O Lord Maheśvara, let the power of this sacred field be told."
I truly wish to hear about those holy places that are worthy of veneration and those lingas that exist; for my curiosity is indeed great. (9)
Īśvara said: Listen with diligence, O Goddess, to the power that destroys sins; it is my foremost sacred field, O Great Goddess, and is always exceedingly dear to me.
And there exists the supreme, greatly meritorious river that removes all sins, as well as the holy and divine Gandhavatī, beloved of the nine rivers.
The Nīlagangā is proclaimed as the fourth and most excellent of rivers; that man who bathes at the confluence of these and performs a śrāddha ceremony, [attains great merit]. (12)
O Goddess, O lady of excellent vows, know that the sacred field of Avantī, extending for one yojana, bestows the fruits of the four aims of life and is three times more meritorious than the Gaṅgā.
There stand the Siddha-liṅgas which bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation; there are eighty-four Īśvaras as well as eight Bhairavas.
Likewise, the eleven Rudras and the twelve Ādityas are recorded; there are six Vināyakas here, and twenty-four Mothers. (15)
When I had gone there to the auspicious Mahākālavana, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and all the others arrived there filled with joy.
O Goddess, this field, extending for one yojana, is pervaded by these; Viṣṇu, the destroyer of all sins, resides in ten locations therein.
The man who recites these names with devotion at dawn, being liberated from all sins, goes to the world of Rudra. || 16 ||
Umā said: "Regarding those eighty-four Liṅgas which have been mentioned by you here, please describe them in detail, for they are the removers of all sins. (19)

Hara said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare their names to you. First among them, renowned upon the earth, is the supreme Agastyeśvara; by the mere sight of whom a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose. 20.
Umā said: "How indeed was this name 'Agastyeśvara' obtained by him? In what place and how did it come to be? You should tell me in detail. (21)
Hara said: Listen, O illustrious goddess, to this ancient narrative, which pacifies all sins and bestows the fruits of one's desires. 22.

Formerly, O Goddess, the gods were defeated by the Asuras and became devoid of energy; all their shares were seized, the ancestors were rendered hopeless, and having lost their sovereignty, the gods then wandered upon the surface of the earth.
Then, on one occasion, those distressed women beheld Agastya, who was endowed with great ascetic power, blazing with the splendor of the sun and possessed of immense vows.
Then, having saluted him and seeing that he was enveloped in splendor, the gods spoke these words to the high-souled Agastya, who is world-renowned: || 25 ||
"Defeated in battle by the Dānavas, we have all been cast down from heaven; therefore, O bull among sages, protect us from this intense fear. (26)
Thus addressed by the gods, Agastya then became enraged; the radiant one blazed forth like the fire of time at the end of an aeon.
Then, O Great Goddess, the Dānavas were scorched by the mass of blazing rays and fell from the sky by the thousands.
Then, being scorched by the splendor of that Agastya and by the power of the sage, all those Daityas and Dānavas fled to Pātāla out of fear.
Then the high-souled Agastya, having slain them, was overcome with grief; his mind agitated by anxiety, he became exceedingly distressed.

"A terrible and great sin has been committed by me in that the Dānavas were slain; for non-violence is the supreme dharma, as stated by Manu. What shall I do? Where shall I go? And how may I be purified? (31)
As he was reflecting thus, his grandfather arrived; he spoke there to the sage: "Why are you overwhelmed with grief?"
"O tiger among sages, you appear [distressed]; let the cause be told quickly. Having paid homage to Brahmā, he spoke to the one who was questioning him.
"O God of gods, O Lord of the universe, my mind is burning within because the sin of killing a Brahmin has come upon me for having slain the Dānavas. (34)
O best of gods, out of favor, tell me the means [to achieve my goal]; O Lord, the ascetic merit I have accumulated over a long time has gone to ruin. (35)
The best of gods spoke this: "Listen with diligence to the supreme means by which the destruction of all sins will certainly come to pass. (36)
In the divine Mahākālavana, frequented by Yakṣas and Gandharvas, there is that unsurpassed Liṅga located to the north of Vaṭayakṣiṇī.
Situated to the south of the Piśāca-tīrtha, by worshipping that [deity], one shall attain the destruction of all sin. || 38 ||
"Worship the auspicious Liṅga that destroys all sins. The righteous-souled one replied, "So be it," and went to Mahākālavana.
O Goddess of the gods, in that linga, the sage became intent on propitiation day and night, devoted with faith and solely absorbed in meditation upon it. || 40 ||
O Goddess, I was then pleased with that high-souled sage.
"O illustrious sage, I have spoken; listen with a concentrated mind. O best of Brahmins, choose a boon, whatever resides in your heart. (42)
I am pleased by this devotion and by your difficult penance; through the power of this liṅga, you have now become stainless.
